news.Title: Alphabet vs. Amazon: Which Is the Better AI Cloud Stock to Own for the Next 5 Years?
news.Content:
Investors view artificial intelligence (AI) as a major technological trend that will shape the global economy. The top AI labs, OpenAI and Anthropic, are reporting soaring revenue and token usage. This confirms that the industry still has momentum.

Further upstream, cloud computing platforms like Alphabet 's (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG) Google Cloud and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) Web Services (AWS) have benefited financially, as their data centers and related ecosystems power consumer and enterprise AI adoption. These are two of the leading hyperscalers that sit at the center of the AI boom. And investors are putting more weight on these segments to judge how their underlying businesses are performing.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Which cloud stock is the best one to own for the next five years?

The cloud businesses are booming

Neither Alphabet nor Amazon is being cautious with their investment approaches. The Google parent plans to spend $200 billion (at the midpoint) in capital expenditures (capex) this year, which will rise meaningfully in 2027. Amazon's capex is expected to total $220 billion in 2026. This money is going toward building technical infrastructure to service the strong demand their cloud platforms are seeing.

On the Q3 2026 earnings call, Andy Jassy, Amazon's chief executive officer, said that "having the leading functionality, security, and operational performance can't help but drive customers to run their apps and store their data in AWS." It has had top market share in the cloud industry for a long time.

But its smaller rival is chipping away at its leadership position. AWS posted year-over-year revenue growth of 39% last quarter, its fastest increase in almost five years. Google Cloud has been expanding at a brisker pace, though, with sales in Q3 up 103% compared to the same period last year. In the third quarter of 2021, its revenue represented 31% of what AWS generated. That figure is now 67%, meaning it has gained substantial market share.

If it was possible to directly own the cloud segments, I'd pick Google Cloud as the better investment opportunity. Not only is revenue rising at a faster clip, but its operating income is skyrocketing as it builds a cost advantage. The backlog is massive at $561 billion, which is slightly lower than the $578 billion that AWS has.

Story Continues

What about the other segments?

While their cloud divisions draw a lot of the market's attention, these are giant technology enterprises that have sprawling operations in different industries. Investors assessing them with a five-year time horizon can't ignore the rest of these businesses.

The biggest question mark facing Alphabet right now might be Google Search, which historically has been its crown jewel. Revenue growth decelerated to 12% in the third quarter.

Queries rose at the fastest rate in five years, but monetization is clearly facing pressure. It's hard to predict the long-term financial impact AI will have on Google Search, but it's certainly not time to panic.

YouTube continues to dominate streaming, and Waymo is significantly ahead of Tesla when it comes to autonomous miles driven.

Amazon sits atop the retail sector. The scale it's built, paired with a massive and well-functioning logistics network, is under no threat. But growth and margins are substantially lower than cloud.

Advertising is a high-margin revenue stream. Investors might be unfamiliar with the fact that Amazon brought in almost $80 billion in annualized ad sales in the third quarter.

Cloud and AI get all the headlines. However, these other segments matter tremendously.

Valuation makes the answer obvious

Despite the AI fears on Google Search, I'd argue Alphabet wins by a nose as the higher-quality company, even though Amazon is also one of the world's elite businesses. The next variable to consider is valuation. Alphabet is more attractive in this area, too.

Its shares trade 27% off their peak (as of Nov. 13), so investors can take advantage of weaker market sentiment to start a position in the company. The stock sells at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 19.9, which is cheaper than Amazon's 24.7 multiple. Getting in at a lower valuation can add to returns.

Alphabet is the better stock to own for the next five years.

news.Title: Worried About Nvidia? 3 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks That May Be Safer Buys Right Now
news.Content:
Nvidia has been in a tailspin over the past week as the uncertainty around who will run its business now that Jensen Huang has resigned as president and CEO is weighing on its valuation. In just the past month, it has declined by nearly 30%. It's an unnerving situation, and there are no guarantees things will get better in the weeks ahead.

For artificial intelligence (AI) investors , there are three tech stocks that may be more attractive options to consider right now: Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG)(NASDAQ:GOOGL), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), and Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO). Here's why I'd go with these stocks today, rather than Nvidia.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Alphabet

Alphabet is an underrated tech stock that I don't think the market is valuing fairly. Given how diverse its business is and how many opportunities it has related to AI, it's a bit surprising to see it trail Nvidia in valuation.

While Alphabet is among the most valuable companies in the world, its market cap of $3.4 trillion remains lower than Nvidia's $3.7 trillion valuation.

The company has a dominant position in online search (Google) and video sharing (YouTube), plus exciting opportunities related to robotaxis (Waymo) and AI chatbots (Gemini).

There's so much potential for Alphabet that it can tap into related to AI that it virtually makes it a no-brainer buy, especially when you consider its modest valuation. At a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of a little under 20, this is a stock that trades in line with the average S&P 500 stock. Except, Alphabet is clearly not average, and it's worthy of a far higher premium.

Amazon

Another AI stock that I believe should be worth more is Amazon. At $2.8 trillion in market cap, its valuation is far lower than Alphabet's. It too is a stock that may have far more room to rise higher.

Amazon's business dominates e-commerce and sets the trend for fast shipping speeds. It's shown that it can fend off low-cost competition by offering its own competitive service, Amazon Haul, to help appeal to price-conscious shoppers.

Its business continues to perform well, with Amazon reporting 12% revenue growth for the September quarter and its cloud business, Amazon Web Services, performing even better with a growth rate of 39%.

Amazon's been getting into the chip-building business and may one day carve out some decent market share for itself. CEO Andy Jassy said if it were a stand-alone operation, it could be bringing in $50 billion in annual sales. Amazon, however, could likely scale that significantly higher.

Story Continues

This is another cheap-looking stock worth buying right now, as its forward P/E multiple is just 24. That's higher than Alphabet, but it still offers great value for the growth opportunities the business possesses.

Broadcom

Chipmaker Broadcom is another stock that I think is a good buy. I haven't always felt that way in the past, as I felt its valuation was too inflated. However, with the stock declining in recent months, I believe there's much more value here now, and it's a much safer investment with less downside risk.

Broadcom builds custom chips that have been in high demand amid the AI tech build-out. Its operations aren't as diverse as Amazon's or Alphabet's, but given how well the business has been doing, it's hard not to like Broadcom's stock.

In its most recent quarter, which ended on Aug. 2, revenue rose by 86% year over year, totaling $29.6 billion. And its growth rate is expected to rise to 93% for the last quarter of its fiscal year. It's a growth beast, and with demand for custom chips on the rise, this could be one of the best AI stocks to own today.

Broadcom's stock is down 2% this year, but it's fallen more than 30% from its 52-week high of $495. It's trading at a forward P/E of 18, making this another attractive stock to buy and hold.

news.Title: Ken Fisher Portfolio Review: 5 Highest-Conviction Technology Stocks for Long-Term Growth
news.Content:
Ken Fisher, founder and former CEO of Fisher Asset Management , has historically maintained a constructive, growth-oriented view of technology stocks. His investment philosophy centers around companies with strong long-term growth potential and competitive advantages.

Technology has been an important part of his investment thesis, particularly large-cap companies with exposure to software, semiconductors, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence. Additionally, Fisher Asset Management favors technology companies with strong intellectual property, established ecosystems, and pricing power that can sustain growth over time.

Ken Fisher has historically maintained an overly optimistic outlook on global equities. Early in the year, he argued that stocks were on course to deliver another strong year but slightly lower than in 2025. Take a look at the 12 best NASDAQ growth stocks to buy .

According to Fisher, global stocks have largely performed as he expected, though the first half of the year was stronger than anticipated. While he did not forecast the conflict in Iran and rate hikes, these events are unlikely to disrupt his full-year outlook.

"Now I want to take you back to something I said earlier and try to put that into perspective. The tech world in aggregate, on average, is doing about 4% better year- to-date than the US as a whole, which includes the tech part as its biggest weight," Fisher said.

In the latest filing, Fisher Asset Management reported approximately $348.3 billion in US reportable holdings. Technology stocks accounted for about 28.2% of the total reported portfolio. Explore 10 Best Tech Stocks for the Next 5 Years .

With that in mind, we have taken a close look at Fisher Asset Management's portfolio and detailed the largest technology stocks with long-term growth trends. We published the Ken Fisher Portfolio Review: 10 Highest-Conviction Technology Stocks for Long-Term Growth . You can find the top 5 stocks below.

Our Methodology

To compile a list of "Ken Fisher Portfolio Review: 10 Highest-Conviction Technology Stocks for Long-Term Growth," we analyzed Fisher Asset Management's Q3 2026 13F portfolio. From the list, we settled on the 10 largest tech companies with solid long-term growth trends. We analyzed why these stocks are poised for growth and detailed how many hedge funds hold stakes in them in Q2 2026. Finally, we ranked the stocks in ascending order based on Fisher Asset Management's equity stake.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

Story Continues

5. Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 369

Fisher Asset Management Equity Stake: $8.86 Billion

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) is a compelling long-term technology investment because it combines several powerful growth engines: Amazon Web Services (AWS), artificial intelligence (AI), digital advertising, and its global e-commerce ecosystem. For more AI investment ideas, see 'Baby Berkshire' Portfolio: 10 Best AI Stocks to Buy According to Warren Buffett Disciple Tom Gayner .

AWS is arguably the most important long-term growth driver, as businesses increasingly move workloads to cloud platforms and invest in AI infrastructure. Revenue in the segment was up 39.3% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 to $46 billion, while operating income rose to $17.8 billion from $11.4 billion a year ago. Explore Amazon stock valuation .

Amazon.com, Inc. is also investing heavily in AI infrastructure and services, including custom AI chips, generative AI models, and enterprise AI solutions. These investments are expected to create additional revenue opportunities. Amazon's advertising business remains an important part of its long-term growth strategy, helping diversify revenue beyond e-commerce and cloud computing. Advertising services revenue reached $19.64 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up 11% year over year from $17.7 billion, or 12% excluding foreign exchange effects.

Meanwhile, e-commerce operations provide another long-term advantage through an enormous customer base, logistics network, Prime membership, and marketplace ecosystem. The North American segment alone generated $112.9 billion in Q3 2026 revenue, while operating income increased 82% year over year to $8.7 billion.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s combination of cloud computing leadership, AI infrastructure investments, advertising opportunities, and improving retail profitability makes it a compelling candidate for long-term technology growth.

4. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 273

Fisher Asset Management Equity Stake: $13.92 Billion

Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) is a high-conviction technology stock for long-term growth, supported by its dominant position in enterprise software, rapidly expanding cloud-computing business, and artificial intelligence investments.

The company is particularly attractive for long-term investors as it does not rely on a single technology trend. Instead, it has multiple growth engines, including Azure, Microsoft 365, Copilot, cybersecurity, and enterprise AI infrastructure.

Microsoft Azure business is a key growth engine as demand for cloud computing continues to grow. Revenue in the unit grew 41% in fiscal 2026, surpassing $100 billion for the first time. Artificial intelligence is also creating additional monetization opportunities through Microsoft 365 Copilot, Azure AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Explore Microsoft's record quarter driven by Azure demand surge.

Strong financial performance supports Microsoft Corporation's prospects as a long-term investment. Revenue in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 was up 19% to $92.3 billion as net income increased 32% to $36.6 billion. The increase was driven by a 30% increase in Microsoft Cloud revenue to $63.9 billion as Azure revenue increased 48% in the quarter.

Wall Street is also optimistic about Microsoft Corporation's long-term prospects, as Scotiabank reiterated its Outperform rating on the stock on October 29 and raised the price target to $650 from $625. On October 30, Baird also raised its price target by $100 to $600, impressed by the third-quarter results, and reiterated an Outperform rating.

3. Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 275

Fisher Asset Management Equity Stake: $13.99 Billion

Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) stands out as a high-conviction long-term technology investment because of its dominant position in digital advertising, expanding cloud-computing business, and substantial artificial intelligence investments. The company is positioning itself as a leading AI company through its Gemini models, Google DeepMind, and AI integration across its products.

Google Cloud revenue increased approximately 103% year over year to $30.7 billion in the third quarter, while operating income surged to $11.1 billion from $3.6 billion a year earlier, highlighting the segment's improving profitability amid rising enterprise AI demand.

The advertising business remains the foundation of its financial strength. Google Search and other advertising revenue increased 12% to $63.3 billion, while YouTube advertising revenue increased 9% to $11.2 billion. Is Alphabet a stock to retire on ?

Strong Cash generation supports long-term investments and reinforces its status as a high-conviction technology stock for long-term growth. In Q3, net cash provided by operating activities totaled $42.3 billion, while operating income rose to $40.6 billion from $31.2 billion a year ago.

For long-term investors, Alphabet Inc.'s appeal is that it is not simply an AI investment. It is an established technology company with multiple revenue streams that can potentially benefit from the growing adoption of AI, cloud computing, and digital services.

2. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 169

Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) has affirmed its status as a high-conviction technology stock for long-term growth amid the broader technology stock sell-off. The stock is up about 26% for the year, outperforming the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100, which is up about 7% over the same period.

The outperformance comes as investors view the company as a defensive, cash-generative technology business with a loyal customer base, strong pricing power, and recurring services revenue. Unlike many AI infrastructure and semiconductor stocks, it benefits from an established global ecosystem that generates substantial cash flow even when technology-sector sentiment deteriorates.

The services business is a key growth engine. Apple Inc. generated approximately $123.3 billion in services revenue, compared with $109.2 billion in fiscal 2025, representing growth of approximately 13%. The business is strategically important because services can generate revenue from Apple's existing customer base without requiring customers to purchase new hardware as frequently.

The underlying business also continues to demonstrate resilience, with the company posting a 12% increase in fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue of $114.5 billion as diluted earnings per share increased 14% to $2.10. Full-year revenue came in at $478.83 billion, up from $416.16 billion in fiscal 2025. Here's why Billionaire Ken Fisher and Jim Cramer Still Like Apple (AAPL) .

According to Wells Fargo, Apple Inc. is well positioned to benefit as investors rotate away from speculative AI stocks amid concerns of elevated valuations and massive infrastructure spending.

1. NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA )

While the stock is down about 39% from its 2026 highs, it remains a long-term growth stock with a competitive advantage in AI accelerators, particularly graphics processing units (GPUs). The stock has come under pressure following Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, with CFO Colette Kress taking over on an interim basis. Investors are now looking toward NVIDIA's November 17 earnings report for reassurance about the stock, but what could drive Nvidia's next phase of growth?

Financial performance demonstrates why it remains one of the most compelling companies in the technology sector. Revenue in the second quarter was up 106% to $96.2 billion, driven by a 117% increase in data center revenue. Net income also rose 126%.

NVIDIA Corporation's long-term prospects hinge on technology companies investing heavily in computing capacity. news.Title: How to Play OKLO Stock as Oklo Secures Key Fuel Supply for Its Ohio Plant
news.Content:
Advanced nuclear technology company Oklo (OKLO) recently signed multiple definitive, multi-year contracts with Centrus Energy (LEU), securing a supply of high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU). This deal formalizes the letter of intent the companies had signed back in June and includes enough HALEU to support up to five Aurora powerhouses for multiple years.

The company's HALEU purchase is supported by a prepayment from Meta Platforms (META) for future Oklo power production and secures fuel for the first phase of Oklo's planned 1.2 GW power campus in Ohio. Oklo believes that these fuel supply agreements would help scale its power business beyond its first reactor and other Aurora deployments.

More News from Barchart

Crude Oil Prices Tumble as Global Supply Concerns Ease

Dollar Strength and Ample Global Supplies Weigh on Crude Oil Prices

Nat-Gas Prices Slip on Forecasts for Warmer US Weather

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

In addition, the company signed a strategic manufacturing agreement with U.S. Forged Rings (USFR) to secure future domestic production of large components for its Aurora powerhouses. This helps address a bottleneck for future deployments as reserved domestic capacity comes online for large components within the Aurora reactor module system.

Oklo also updated investors on its Groves Isotope Test Reactor (Groves-1), which received clearance for the final operations hold point from the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) through the Reactor Pilot Program (RPP). With this, the facility can move into its research, testing, and training phase.

As the company looks toward expansion, it may be wise to explore it. However, markets have turned a bit sour on Oklo's growth prospects, leading to a selloff in its stock over the past year. Therefore, it might be wise to wait for a better trigger point.

About OKLO Stock

Oklo is a nuclear energy company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It develops small, fast-fission power plants called Aurora powerhouses. These plants are designed to produce clean, reliable electricity and heat for data centers, factories, remote communities, and military sites. Oklo also recycles used nuclear fuel into new fuel and produces important isotopes. Its goal is to make clean nuclear energy more affordable and available at a larger scale. The company has a market capitalization of $4.67 billion.

Story Continues

Oklo's stock has fallen about 76% over the past 52 weeks because investors have become less excited about its high-growth plans. The company's shares rose sharply when people expected AI data centers to need large amounts of clean nuclear power. But as confidence in AI infrastructure spending weakened, investors lowered their expectations for Oklo's future growth. Over the past six months, OKLO stock has dropped 70%. It reached a 52-week low of $18.53 on Nov. 5, but is up 20% from that level. Despite the steep selloff, the stock's valuation remains sky-high.

Oklo Reported Q3 Results as It Advances Reactor Development

For the third quarter, Oklo generated $1.86 million in revenue. However, losses also climbed in tandem. Its net loss per share climbed from $0.20 in Q3 2025 to $0.22 in Q3 2026. For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Oklo exited the period with $1.63 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash. This was mainly due to financing activities, including $2.30 billion raised in the first three quarters through successful ATM offerings.

Wall Street analysts are pessimistic about Oklo's bottom-line trajectory. For fiscal 2026, the company's loss per share is expected to widen 37.5% year-over-year (YoY) to $0.99, followed by another 24.2% increase to $1.23 in fiscal 2027. For the fourth quarter, loss per share is expected to increase 3.7% YoY to $0.28.

What Do Analysts Think About OKLO Stock?

This month, Truist Securities analyst Christopher Souther maintained a "Hold" rating on OKLO stock and cut the price target from $31 to $28. Canaccord Genuity analysts also maintained a "Buy" rating on the stock but reduced the price target from $100 to $66. HC Wainwright & Co. reiterated its rating, with analyst Sameer Joshi maintaining a "Buy" rating. The price target remains steady at $90. Based on recent analyst stances, there is cautious optimism around Oklo.

OKLO stock remains well liked on Wall Street, with analysts awarding it a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating. Of the 24 analysts rating the stock, 11 have given it a "Strong Buy" rating, two have suggested a "Moderate Buy," and 11 have taken a middle-of-the-road approach with a "Hold" rating.  The consensus price target of $60.76 represents a 173% upside from current levels. Moreover, the Street-high price target of $130 implies a 484% upside.

news.Title: Marvell Just Made a Massive Move Against Broadcom. How to Play MRVL Stock Now.
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) has decided that winning the AI infrastructure race takes more than designing faster chips. Its $115 billion agreement to acquire Lumentum (LITE) is a bid to control more of the connections that make enormous AI systems work. This move brings Broadcom (AVGO) into the picture and increases the risks for Marvell's shareholders. Here's how it could play out.

MRVL stock is up 71% so far this year, beating the S&P 500 Index ($SPX), whereas AVGO stock is down about 3%.

More News from Barchart

Jensen Huang Said 'Nothing Would Give Me More Joy' Than Paying Higher Taxes and Called Owing $8 Billion a 'Privilege'

Dear MicroStrategy Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 30

Walmart Gets $2.9 Billion in Tariff Refunds, Ford $1.3 Billion, and Apple $2.2 Billion: The Average Household Paid an Estimated $700 and Got Nothing

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

Marvell Wants a Bigger Place in the AI Stack

Marvell's $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum aims to unite two vital pillars of AI infrastructure into a single powerhouse. This all-stock deal merges Marvell's custom AI accelerators, cutting-edge interconnects, networking switches, and semiconductor expertise with Lumentum's high-performance lasers, advanced optical transceivers, and optical circuit switching. Lumentum additionally contributes its specialized compound semiconductor manufacturing, including indium phosphide technology, a key ingredient for next-generation optical components.

After the deal closes, current Marvell investors will likely own about two-thirds of the new company, while Lumentum investors own the rest. Because the deal uses a fixed share-exchange ratio, changes in Marvell's stock price before the deal closes will affect how much Lumentum shareholders receive. Both groups of shareholders face market swings during the long approval process. The risk impacts everyone.

Marvell expects this merger will create a broader connectivity portfolio, covering everything from links between data centers and servers to connections between processors within advanced AI systems. With this bold move, the company believes the combined business could tap into a $550 billion market opportunity, generating over $1 billion in annual cost synergies and boosting long-term revenue and margins. Marvell forecasts that the acquisition will begin adding to its adjusted EPS in the first year after completion. The companies are targeting a closing in early 2028, subject to regulatory clearance and shareholder approval.

Story Continues

So how does Broadcom fit into this? Broadcom stands out as a strong rival, powering hyperscalers' vast data centers with its custom AI accelerators and networking silicon. Marvell operates in overlapping markets, including custom silicon, switching, and connectivity. The main idea is to move data, not just process it. AI accelerators need fast connections to communicate with each other, as well as with storage and networking gear. Copper is still useful, but as systems scale, distance, bandwidth, and power become bigger issues. Optical technology can send data farther and faster, and often does so more efficiently. Marvell already offers optical digital signal processors, interconnects, and switches. Lumentum adds advanced lasers, optical transceivers, switching technology, and specialized semiconductor manufacturing. According to Reuters , Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum signals its intent to challenge Broadcom more aggressively for a share of AI investment.

This is Why Marvell Wants to Move Faster

Marvell's fiscal 2027 second-quarter earnings show why Marvell wants to move faster. Revenue surged to $2.74 billion, a 37% year-over-year (YoY) leap and a 13% jump from the previous quarter. Data center sales soared to $2.17 billion, accounting for 79% of total revenue and up 46% from last year. The real powerhouse behind this momentum is the explosive demand for AI.

Looking ahead, Marvell projects Q3 revenue to hit $3.15 billion at the midpoint, denoting a 15% jump from last quarter and over 50% YoY growth. The company has also boosted its fiscal 2027 revenue target to about $12 billion, up from $11.5 billion, and raised its fiscal 2028 outlook to around $18 billion, up from $16.5 billion, aiming for roughly 50% growth.

Marvell's Q2 adjusted gross margin stood at 58.9%, while adjusted earnings per share climbed 40% YoY to $0.94. CFO Dan Durn said adjusted operating margin was expected to enter the company's 38% to 40% long-term target range as fiscal 2027 progressed.

Management pointed to surging demand across interconnect, switching, and custom silicon. Marvell reported strong demand for its 800-gigabit optical products, while its 1.6-terabit business is gaining momentum. The company expects its 51.2-terabit switching products to more than double this fiscal year. By fiscal 2028, management anticipates data center revenue to soar over 60%, with custom silicon revenue more than doubling. Marvell is also in talks with major customers about scale-up switches, each signifying a potential multibillion-dollar opportunity over their lifetimes.

Marvell ended the quarter with $4.96 billion in debt, but its net debt was low compared to its earnings at just 0.27 times EBITDA. Because Marvell will use its own shares, not cash, to buy Lumentum, current shareholders will own a smaller stake in the combined company. Still, Marvell will have to manage Lumentum's debt and other financial responsibilities while integrating the two businesses and keeping its own operations and growth on track.

How to Play MRVL Stock Now

Marvell has an attractive opportunity to become a bigger player in AI connectivity and challenge Broadcom, but the Lumentum deal raises the execution stakes. Marvell still has to show it can integrate this major acquisition, manage dilution, and turn its new technology into real, profitable growth.

MRVL offers substantial upside, but the acquisition raises the bar for successful integration and growth. Investors confident in Marvell's ability could build exposure gradually around quarterly results and deal updates. More cautious investors might prefer to wait for clearer proof before investing.

Overall, analysts continue to be strongly bullish about MRVL stock. Of the 37 analysts covering the stock, 26 rate it a "Strong Buy," three a "Moderate Buy," and eight a "Hold." Marvell's average price target of $307.88 indicates a possible upside of 111%. The most ambitious forecast of $450 hints at an exciting 208% upside from the current price.

news.Title: Apple's $1,299 iPhone has a problem updates can't fix
news.Content:
Spending $1,299 on a smartphone should mean getting a device that handles the basics. Yet several customers of Apple's most recent high-end iPhone found that they could no longer make phone calls.

They were unable to make calls, send texts, or access mobile internet since their gadgets lost cellular connectivity. And the most unexpected part? A software update was unable to fix it.

In October, Apple (AAPL) acknowledged that a few iPhone 18 Pro Max handsets running on AT&T's (T) network were impacted.

To stop such malfunctions, the business made software and carrier upgrades. But consumers were told they would need new phones if their current phones had already lost service.

Shortly after the iPhone 18 Pro Max went on sale on Sept. 18, the issue surfaced, exposing an awkward contradiction for Apple.

The business uses advancements in cameras, AI, and battery life to market its priciest smartphones. However, several users encountered issues with the function that first made cellphones indispensable: maintaining connectivity.

The story highlights concerns about product dependability, customer service, and what happens when a costly gadget stops working at its most basic level for Americans who pay high rates.

Apple's $1,299 iPhone failure requires replacement

The iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299 in the U.S., according to Apple's September launch announcement. The device has new artificial intelligence functions, longer battery life, and better cameras.

Some AT&T users began reporting ongoing connection issues soon after the introduction.

Related: Apple users are about to lose something they've had for 28 years

Sometimes the affected phones showed SOS mode, which meant that regular cellular service was not available. Users complained about being unable to make calls, send messages, or access mobile data, MacRumors noted.

The outage also raised concerns about emergency communications. AT&T admitted that the problem may impact 911 calls, which elevated the issue beyond a minor annoyance.

Apple later acknowledged the flaw.

In a statement reported by 9to5Mac , the company said it had identified an issue affecting a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T. It did not disclose the number of impacted devices.

Apple also recognized a significant drawback: Updating software would not fix a phone's cellular failure. This meant that rather than using another troubleshooting technique, the affected consumers required new phones.

Apple offers 2 solutions depending on the problem

Early in October, Apple released iOS 27.0.1 along with a different AT&T carrier settings update. The modifications were made to stop other devices from experiencing the same connection issue.

Story Continues

Nevertheless, the upgrades have a different function than swapping out phones that have already broken down.

MacRumors reported Oct. 2 that Apple advised affected customers to contact Apple Support or AT&T, or visit a retail location for a replacement.

The company suggested applying the available updates for clients whose iPhone 18 Pro Max is still operational. By accessing Settings, choosing General, and then Software Update, owners may check for iOS upgrades.

To check AT&T carrier settings, go to Settings, choose General, and then About.

However, rather than hoping that another update would fix the device, consumers whose phones have already lost cellular connectivity should get in touch with Apple or AT&T.

This difference is especially crucial for people who rely on their phones for business, banking, navigation, or emergency communication.

Even if the replacement is covered, malfunctioning equipment might result in costs and inconveniences.

More Apple:

Bank of America doubles down on its Apple stock bet

MKBHD drops a blunt verdict on Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro

Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo is already rewarding buyers who wait

Apple's connectivity problem exposes a surprising difference

The problem is particularly intriguing because of one element.

The Snapdragon X80 cellular modem from Qualcomm (QCOM) powers the iPhone 18 Pro Max in the United States.

The same model sold in other countries uses Apple's own C2 modem. Meanwhile, the smaller iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo use Apple's modem globally.

MacRumors reported Oct. 5 that Apple had observed the connectivity problem only among iPhone 18 Pro Max devices using AT&T.

There is no concrete proof that the breakdown was caused by Qualcomm's modem, and in the examined reports, Apple and AT&T have not provided a public explanation of the problem.

Nevertheless, the various hardware setups show how difficult it is to introduce smartphones across many carriers and foreign countries. In one network arrangement, a device may function dependably, while in another, it may have issues.

This suggests that the dependability of an expensive phone may depend on factors other than the manufacturer's stated standards. It also relies on how its wireless carrier, software, and hardware interact.

Apple's iPhone problem creates a larger question for investors

Apple's financial success is still largely dependent on the iPhone.

Customers that are prepared to spend more for better hardware and features contribute to the company's income generation via its premium models. Because of this, Apple's brand values dependability.

When a consumer spends $1,299 on a device, they want it to perform consistently, particularly its basic communication features.

The specific issue's financial effect is yet unknown, however.

There is no evidence that the issue has significantly impacted iPhone sales or the company's profits, and Apple has characterized the impacted group as tiny. Additionally, the problem has not been verified for Apple's wider range of smartphones.

The top concern for investors is whether Apple can restrict replacement costs, consumer annoyance, and brand harm.

Apple's long-term investment perspective is unlikely to be altered by a single product issue. However, frequent dependability issues may discourage high-end consumers from updating, especially when rival competitors provide comparable features at lower costs.

Another distinction is worth keeping an eye on: Although Apple has not made public the exact number of phones that need to be replaced, its preventive upgrades may lessen the likelihood of future malfunctions.

This raises questions about the problem's broader scope.

A more thorough description of the reason, the number of impacted devices, and whether the remedial updates have stopped further instances would be the next significant advance.

The immediate takeaway is more obvious for American customers. Instead of depending on frequent software updates, anyone with an impacted iPhone 18 Pro Max should contact Apple or AT&T for help.

The incident serves as a warning to Apple that even the most advanced smartphones must initially excel at something far less glamorous than artificial intelligence.

They have to work as phones.

news.Title: Alphabet, Amazon, and Nvidia All Have a Stake in Anthropic. Here’s the One I’d Buy If I Could Only Pick 1.
news.Content:
Anthropic is planning to go public around Nov. 19. This will be a huge deal for the market, as its valuation will be north of $1 trillion. Many early investors will benefit from it going public, including companies like Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL), and Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA). All three of these businesses invested in Anthropic when it was private and are in for a major windfall now that it's going public.

But of these three stocks, which one is the best pick? Or should you buy Anthropic itself? Let's take a look.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Anthropic's growth rates are incredible

First, let's look at Anthropic itself. Some of the financials in its S-1 document are downright incredible. For the first six months of 2026, its revenue grew at a 1,305% year-over-year pace to $16.3 billion. That easily crushes the growth that Amazon, Alphabet, and Nvidia are putting up.

NVDA Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts

So, from a pure growth standpoint, Anthropic is the best buy . However, that's not all there is with a company. Anthropic is deeply unprofitable, although a large chunk of its $80 billion net loss over the first six months of the year is due to accounting artifacts.

However, it lost about $700 million from operations in the first six months of the year, which isn't a huge loss to overcome. So, Anthropic is very close to becoming a viable company on its own, which makes it a smart investment. But is it better than these other three that are established stalwarts in the artificial intelligence (AI) industry?

The big tech landscape is shifting

A month ago, if you asked me what the best buy between Nvidia, Amazon, and Alphabet would be, I wouldn't have hesitated to say Nvidia. However, with its CEO in the hot seat over two affairs, there is a lot less certainty.

Its business is still quite certain, as its graphics processing units (GPUs) are best in class and are utilized by companies like Anthropic to train and run AI models around Nvidia's leadership. Nvidia's stake in Anthropic is the smallest of the three, which also means it has the least to gain.

Alphabet may seem like an odd company to invest in Anthropic because it's openly competing against it with its Gemini family of AI models. However, Alphabet is an important Anthropic partner and hosts a lot of its workload on Google Cloud. This gives Alphabet multiple bets in the AI space, as it doesn't need its own AI platform to work out (although it would prefer that).

Story Continues

Next is Amazon, which is in a similar boat to Alphabet. Amazon isn't developing its own AI model. Instead, it's choosing to stay neutral and just host other companies' models. Amazon has been a longtime Anthropic investor and has hosted its workloads for years. Anthropic is also training some of its AI models using Amazon's proprietary chips. Amazon needs Anthropic to be successful for its AI bets to work out, so it has a lot riding on Anthropic's initial public offering (IPO).

So, of the three, which makes the best buy? I think it's Alphabet. Alphabet has a great relationship with Anthropic, although it doesn't need Anthropic to pan out due to its in-house AI model. Amazon needs Anthropic to be successful; otherwise, one of its largest clients is gone. While I usually prefer to invest in companies like Nvidia that are neutral hardware suppliers, the market's reaction to its CEO's resignation has me concerned, and I think it's best to stay patient with that stock right now.

We'll see how Anthropic's IPO goes shortly, and the reality is that all three stocks will benefit from it, but I think Alphabet has the edge right now.

news.Title: Why Intel Stock Just Dropped
news.Content:
Pity Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) investors. Not only have they had to deal with the fallout of an Nvidia CEO scandal not of their making this month -- one that's contributed to an 18% drop in stock price in November alone.

Not only are they now struggling to parse a new SemiAnalysis report warning that capital spending on AI chips in 2027 could be 19% below previous estimates, 2028 spending might be 28% below, and 2029 spending could fall 41 % below estimates.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Today, Intel investors are facing yet another negative catalyst for their stock. Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), it seems, is selling down its stake in its semiconducting rival -- and it's costing Intel stock a 2.3% decline through 1:30 p.m. ET today.

Image source: Intel.

Nvidia cashes out

Nvidia just confirmed in an SEC filing that it has sold 25% of its Intel stock position, reducing its stake from 214.8 million shares to 161.1 million. At the same time, as StreetInsider.com reports, Nvidia has increased its ownership in SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) by 6%, to 130.5 million shares.

All of these numbers are as of Sept. 30, before the Jensen Huang scandal broke.

What's next for Intel

Nvidia's moves proved prescient. Although SpaceX stock has fallen slightly since the report date (down about 6%), Intel shares are down much, much more -- roughly 55%. So Nvidia kept a lot of its Intel profits by cashing out before Intel crashed (a crash that Nvidia's own CEO scandal helped cause).

The question for Intel investors now is: should you follow Nvidia's example and sell out of Intel, too? Before you do that, recall that if Nvidia sold 25% of its Intel shares in September, then it also kept 75%.

So Nvidia hasn't abandoned all hope in Intel yet. Maybe you shouldn't either ?

news.Title: There's 'no difference' between buying Anthropic's IPO and Amazon's IPO: Kevin O'Leary
news.Content:
As Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) prepares to begin trading under the ticker ANT on Thursday, Nov. 19, business leaders are weighing in on the historically large initial public offering (IPO).

"There's no difference in investing in Anthropic on the IPO than Amazon on its IPO," "Shark Tank" host and O'Leary Ventures chair Kevin O'Leary said on Sozzi Unleashed . "There was tremendous volatility. It made zero money. But look at the platform it ultimately built. That's what you're betting on in the Anthropic deal."

Sitting down with Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi, O'Leary said the past few years haven't been great for buying IPOs, but he believes Anthropic may be a unique way to bet on artificial intelligence.

Anthropic said it expects to sell 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78 each. That would give the company a market valuation of between $1.3 trillion and $1.45 trillion — putting it near SpaceX's ( SPCX ) IPO valuation of $1.77 trillion, which was the largest ever.

"It may be the most hyped IPO ever," O'Leary said. "This IPO is the anchor to the entire AI or SI trade, whatever you want to call it."

What about the fact that Anthropic may not turn a profit until 2030? Though Anthropic's operating losses have improved, they still total $1.3 billion for the first nine months of the year. The company also noted in its amended IPO filing that it plans to spend nearly $900 billion on computing and data centers, with $70 billion of that total coming due within a year.

O'Leary said Anthropic's profitability is the wrong lens right now. Buying in is a bet on AI's role across all 11 sectors of the economy, and he sees evidence of productivity and margin gains so far. That has helped markets remain near all-time highs despite tariffs, wars, and high energy prices.

These remarks follow O'Leary's comments last month, when the businessman called Anthropic "a hot trade."

"I expect it to be liquid from day one, and that changes the opportunity," he wrote in October.

news.Title: TSMC Stocks Fall 4.26% as New US Rule Tightens Checks on Chip Foundries
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( NYSE:TSM ) shares fell 4.26% at 10:45 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, after the Commerce Department unveiled a rule that tightens how foundries and packagers handle advanced logic chips. Reuters reported that TSMC and Samsung shares lost ground in Asia as the measure raised due diligence and licensing burdens for foundries serving Chinese fabless companies.

Is TSM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The interim final rule keeps the presumption that certain advanced logic chips are controlled and narrows how fabricators can overcome it when the designer is located in, or headquartered in, a restricted destination. It adds a license requirement for such chips from designers that are neither approved nor authorized when a front-end fabricator or packager exports them. It also requires licenses for advanced chips sent to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, effective on publication scheduled for November 19.

For TSMC the likely cost is customer screening and slower approvals rather than lost leading-edge demand, since its biggest advanced-node customers are US designers such as Nvidia and AMD. Smaller Chinese design wins could still be delayed. GuruFocus gives TSMC a GF Score of 99/100, near perfect across profitability, balance sheet strength and momentum. Its GF Value of $383.04 implies a 4% discount, which GuruFocus rates fairly valued, so quality is priced in but not stretched. The next test is TSMC's November revenue report and any sign of license-related delays.

news.Content: 台股17日賣壓持續湧現，加權指數終場下跌947.97點，收在40,092.11點，跌幅2.31%，驚險守住4萬點大關，成交金額達9,617.95億元。由於市場盛傳輝達（NVIDIA）新一代AI平台Vera Rubin遭遇技術瓶頸、放量時程恐延後至2027年上半年，引爆資金大舉撤出高本益比零組件，PCB、ABF載板與銅箔基板（CCL）等「AI材料股」連兩日淪為超級提款機；不過， 高階PCB廠金像電（2368）與CCL龍頭台光電（2383） 盤中已驚現低接買盤進場承接！ 【Vera Rubin傳兩大瓶頸 供應鏈說法分歧待輝達定調】 這波「AI材料股大逃殺」的導火線，源自供應鏈傳出Vera Rubin平台面臨雙重製造難題。除了國內消息指稱新一代高頻寬記憶體（HBM4）良率與供應吃緊、研調機構TrendForce評估恐延至2027年上半年才逐步放量外，外媒《Newsquawk》也引述研究機構說法，指出大尺寸晶片與主機板出現翹曲（Warpage）現象影響良率；不過該消息同時聲稱HBM問題10月已解決，顯示業界對卡關原因說法分歧，且均未獲輝達官方證實。 【載板三雄全面躺平！金像電、台光電盤中驚現低接買盤】 受遞延傳聞衝擊，市場原本期待M9高階銅箔基板與高層數載板升級的資金大舉撤出。ABF載板三雄首當其衝， 南電（8046）開盤即打入跌停792元並跌破年線；剛出關的景碩（3189） 同樣亮燈跌停鎖死542元； 欣興（3037）早盤也一度觸及跌停637元，盤中跌幅逾9%。此外，博智（8155）、鑽針廠尖點（8021）及玻纖布廠富喬（1815） 、 建榮（5340） 、 南亞（1303）與被動元件雙雄國巨（2327） 、 華新科（2492） 全數承壓。 在一片慘綠之中，具備業績實績的 金像電（2368）早盤跳空觸及跌停835元後，盤中湧現低接買盤拉抬，跌幅一度收斂至約7%；CCL龍頭台光電（2383）開盤逼近跌停後同樣吸引承接買盤進場，股價回升至3,470元附近，反觀同族群的台燿（6274）與聯茂（6213） 則延續弱勢。相較之下， 鴻海（2317）與廣達（2382） 因主力GB300伺服器已進入大量交貨期，營運受影響相對有限。 【明晨輝達法說會成關鍵 法人揭3大止跌反彈指標】 展望後市，市場全數屏息等待台灣時間18日清晨5時20分公布的輝達財報，以及6時由代理執行長柯蕾絲（Colette Kress）主持的法說會。法人指出，此次傳聞恰逢黃仁勳卸任後的接班過渡期，多重雜音放大了恐慌情緒，短線能否止跌反彈需觀察三大指標： 輝達法說會定調： 若官方澄清Vera Rubin進度正常，或證實GB300訂單足以填補空窗期，具備實際出貨實績的台光電與金像電有望率先領軍反彈。 跌停打開與量能： 連續跌停的南電與景碩需先觀察能否爆量打開跌停，已見承接的個股則要觀察後續是否量縮止跌不破低。

news.Title: 台股狂殺239檔受益人出走　它卻逆勢暴增近4萬人！
news.Content:
國安基金日前決議啟動安定市場任務，授權執行秘書視市況動用資金，隨著政府公布穩定市場措施，加上美國科技股回升，台股反彈能否延續，後續可觀察外資賣壓是否緩和，以及企業獲利能否支撐股價。台股11月第一週跌逾5,500點，盤點全台364檔台股ETF中，共有239檔受益人數下降，其中僅112檔呈現正成長，另有部分持平；而國泰永續高股息（00878）單週受益人增加近3.7萬人，為台股被動式高股息ETF之首。00878迎來今年第四次收益分配，昨(17)日除息，預定12月11日發放。

對於11月第一週受益人增量放大，國泰永續高股息（00878）基金經理人江宇騰分析，可從三個面向觀察。首先，台股回檔可能促使原有分批布局計畫的投資人重新評估進場時點；其次，00878迎來今年第四次收益分配，也可能提高投資人對其關注度；第三，00878同時配置金融與科技股，以主要持股中信金與廣達為例，前者的銀行業務涵蓋放款利息與財富管理手續費，後者可觀察AI伺服器訂單與出貨進度。兩類企業的獲利來源不同，讓投資人可在同一組合中兼顧金融與科技配置。

除了00878備受關注之外，另一檔國泰投信旗下共同基金「國泰台灣高股息基金」，基金規模達554.17億元，由經理人梁恩溢主動選股，其中半導體占32.99%、電子零組件占27.75%，合計60.74%，另亦布局電腦及週邊設備、光電、塑膠與金融等產業。科技股反彈後，可觀察企業訂單能否如期轉為出貨、營收成長能否帶動獲利，再評估股價是否已反映成長預期。

面對台股波動，投資人可依自身資金規劃與風險承受度，設定適合的投資金額與期間，透過定期定額持續累積資產，參與金融與科技等不同產業的投資機會。長期投入有助分散單次進場時點的影響，投資人仍應留意市場變化，並衡量自身承受能力。

news.Title: 《強勢美股特報》CHRW,SYK,T,LMT等6檔
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-18 01:08:35 數位內容中心 發佈

C.H. Robinson Worldwide（CHRW.US）： 成交價136.58美元，上漲1.42%，開盤135.14美元，盤中高點137.12美元，盤中低點134.03美元，均價135.99美元，成交量7.43萬股。

C.H. Robinson Worldwide剛宣布收購卡車貨運經紀商RXO，這是近期最直接改變公司營運方向的動作。公司希望在貨運市場偏弱之際，擴大卡車經紀規模，並結合AI提升調度與營運效率。不過，市場同時看到收購後槓桿率將上升，且公司先前提到營運現金流較去年同期下降，主因是運輸費率提高帶來不利的營運資本變化。也就是說，C.H. Robinson Worldwide目前不是單純靠景氣回升推動，而是選擇在景氣壓力下用併購擴張版圖，後續整合成效、現金流修復，以及買賣價差能否改善，會比單季營收是否優於預期更能決定這筆交易的實際價值。

Stryker（SYK.US）： 成交價314.86美元，上漲1.33%，開盤309.12美元，盤中高點319.25美元，盤中低點308.68美元，均價313.58美元，成交量18.06萬股。

Stryker近期以4億美元投資CMR Surgical，並取得Versius手術機器人的美國獨家經銷權，顯示公司正把機器人布局從原本較強的骨科領域，進一步延伸到軟組織手術。這項變化的重點，不是既有骨科器材銷售，而是公司開始補齊另一個手術平台。Stryker原本已擁有Mako系統，如今再透過Versius切入不同類型手術，代表其機器人業務不再侷限單一應用。對醫材公司而言，是否能把裝機、耗材與醫院採用流程串起來，往往比一次性設備銷售更重要。Stryker這次選擇投資加上獨家經銷，而非單純合作，也顯示公司希望更深度參與美國手術機器人市場的擴張。

AT&T（T.US）： 成交價22.67美元，上漲1.36%，開盤22.23美元，盤中高點22.68美元，盤中低點22.19美元，均價22.53美元，成交量225.41萬股。

AT&T近期面對的最大變數，是SpaceX明確加快進軍美國行動通訊市場。SpaceX已達成協議收購一組全國性的800MHz低頻譜執照，並規劃結合衛星連線與地面基礎設施，打造可直接服務一般手機的全國網路，相關交易仍待FCC核准。對AT&T而言，壓力不只來自一個新的衛星業者，而是原本偏向補足訊號死角的技術，正逐步往完整電信服務靠攏。AT&T管理層則強調，衛星訊號在建築物內、高密度場館與企業級服務場景，仍難取代成熟的地面網路，顯示公司正把競爭焦點拉回室內覆蓋、容量與既有基礎設施優勢。換言之，AT&T眼前的變化是競爭邊界被重新劃定，而非短期營運數字的小幅波動。

Lockheed Martin（LMT.US）： 成交價592.07美元，上漲1.17%，開盤584.95美元，盤中高點592.99美元，盤中低點584.95美元，均價588.42美元，成交量5.5萬股。

Lockheed Martin近期公開訊息仍以評級、持股與財報預期為主，未見足以明確改變營運方向的新合約、重大產品進展或財測調整。現有資料較能確認的是，公司下一個主要觀察點仍是即將到來的財報，市場預估該季營收約205億美元、每股盈餘約7.52美元。從基本面描述來看，Lockheed Martin的核心業務仍集中在F-35戰機、飛彈防禦系統與太空系統，營收大部分來自美國政府，代表其營運主線仍是既有國防專案的執行與交付，而不是近期出現新的策略轉折。在缺乏新增公司事件的情況下，市場暫時仍在等待管理層針對專案進度、成長節奏與獲利表現提出下一步更新。

Edison International（EIX.US）： 成交價62.68美元，上漲1.15%，開盤61.12美元，盤中高點63.08美元，盤中低點61.12美元，均價62.39美元，成交量20.21萬股。

Edison International近期最核心的變化仍是加州野火責任風險升高。加州參議院法案SB492未納入市場原先期待的責任保障條款後，公司一度出現25年來最大單日跌幅，反映外界擔心法律防火牆遲遲未建立，未來潛在索賠的損失上限難以評估。更麻煩的是，與Eaton Fire相關的陪審團審判預計到2027年1月才開庭，代表這項不確定性還會持續一段時間。信評展望也已遭下修，顯示問題不只是訴訟本身，還延伸到融資能力與資本成本。對Edison International來說，接下來的營運重點會放在如何在持續投資電網與面對法律風險之間維持財務彈性，而不是單看公用事業需求是否穩定。

T-Mobile US（TMUS.US）： 成交價171.31美元，上漲0.76%，開盤170美元，盤中高點173.92美元，盤中低點169.4美元，均價171.85美元，成交量12.28萬股。

T-Mobile US近期最受矚目的變化，是原本合作的SpaceX正更明確朝全國性電信服務邁進。馬斯克已公開表示，若未來能更有效運用頻譜資源，不排除直接收購大型傳統電信業者。SpaceX也已購入頻譜使用執照，並預計在2028年初啟用初期無線通訊服務，還尋求基地台使用權並與高通合作地面基礎設施技術。對T-Mobile US來說，這使原先由衛星補足死角的合作關係，開始帶有潛在競爭色彩。不過，市場也點出T-Mobile US因已與SpaceX建立合作，在三大業者中反而可能是最自然的整合對象。換句話說，T-Mobile US眼前最大的公司變化，不是既有用戶數的短期起伏，而是與SpaceX之間的關係正從合作逐步走向更複雜的競合。

news.Title: Palantir's 148% U.S. Commercial Revenue Surge Signals AI Momentum
news.Content:
Palantir Technologies Inc. PLTR continues to demonstrate strong growth momentum, supported by accelerating adoption of its artificial intelligence solutions among U.S. businesses. The company's third-quarter 2026 performance highlights the expanding commercial applications of its AI-driven platforms and their growing contribution to overall revenues.

The impressive growth in U.S. commercial revenues strengthens Palantir's long-term expansion prospects, although sustaining this momentum will depend on continued enterprise adoption.

PLTR's U.S. Commercial Business Gains Momentum

Palantir's U.S. commercial revenues surged 148% year over year to $984 million in the third quarter of 2026 from $397 million in the corresponding year-ago period.

This sharp acceleration underscores growing enterprise demand for Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP), which enables businesses to integrate AI into operational workflows and improve decision-making.

Increasing adoption across industries provides opportunities for Palantir to expand existing customer relationships and capture additional enterprise spending. The substantial revenue increase also reflects the company's growing presence in the commercial AI market.

Government Business Reinforces PLTR's Growth

Beyond commercial operations, Palantir's U.S. government business continues to demonstrate considerable strength, providing another source of revenue expansion.

Third-quarter 2026 U.S. government revenues climbed 96% year over year to $953 million from $486 million. This robust performance highlights sustained demand for Palantir's advanced data analytics and AI capabilities across government agencies.

The simultaneous expansion of commercial and government revenues strengthens Palantir's growth profile. However, maintaining such exceptional growth rates could become increasingly challenging as the company's revenue base expands.

How Do PLTR's Peers Compare?

Microsoft Corporation MSFT and Snowflake SNOW are two U.S.-listed companies benefiting from growing enterprise investments in AI and data infrastructure.

Microsoft continues to strengthen its competitive position through Azure AI services and Copilot offerings, enabling organizations to integrate generative AI into everyday business operations. Microsoft's extensive enterprise customer base supports opportunities for broader AI monetization.

Meanwhile, Snowflake is expanding its AI capabilities within its cloud-based data platform, helping enterprises develop applications and extract insights from their information assets. Snowflake's emphasis on data integration and AI-powered analytics positions it to benefit from increasing demand for intelligent enterprise solutions.

Story Continues

PLTR's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

The stock has gained 18.7% in the past six months compared with the industry's 9.6% growth.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

From a valuation standpoint, PLTR trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of 31.45X, well above the industry average of 3.73X. It carries a Value Score of D.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for PLTR's 2026 earnings has increased over the past 60 days.

PLTR stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Meta Platforms is Cheap at 18.78X P/E: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Meta Platforms META shares are cheap, as suggested by the Value Score of B. In terms of the forward 12-month price/earnings (P/E), META is trading at 18.78X, lower than the Zacks Internet Software industry's 26.90X. The social-networking giant is trading at a discount compared with Amazon 's AMZN 23.39X and Microsoft 's MSFT 24.20X. However, Meta Platforms' shares are trading at a premium compared with Alphabet 's GOOGL 18.30X.

META Stock's Valuation

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

So, is Meta stock a buy, sell or hold at this level? Let's find out.

META Suffers From Rising AI Spend

Meta shares have lost 5.1% year to date (YTD), underperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's appreciation of 6.9%, Microsoft's rise of 7.2%, and Amazon's return of 11.7%. However, META shares have outperformed Alphabet shares, which have dropped 9.3% over the same time frame.

META Stock's Price Performance

Meta's aggressive investments in AI infrastructure represent a significant near-term challenge. The company expects 2026 capital expenditures, including finance lease principal payments, of $135-$145 billion, reflecting substantial spending on data centers, servers and networking infrastructure. Capital expenditures reached $34.91 billion in the third quarter compared with $19.37 billion in the year-ago period.

Despite generating $32.79 billion in operating cash flow, Meta reported negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion during the quarter. The company has $454.52 billion in non-cancelable contractual commitments and approximately $355.73 billion in leases that had not yet commenced. These commitments relate primarily to cloud capacity, computing infrastructure, data centers and energy requirements.

Meta's accelerating operating expenses are creating pressure on profitability despite strong revenue growth. In the third quarter of 2026, total costs and expenses surged 68% year over year to $51.61 billion, significantly outpacing revenue growth of 26%. GAAP operating income declined 37% year over year to $12.99 billion, while operating margin contracted to 20% from 40% in the year-ago quarter. Although the results included a $9.89 billion legal settlement charge, increasing infrastructure expenses, third-party cloud spending, depreciation and AI token costs remain underlying concerns. Meta's continued investments in advanced AI models and computing infrastructure are expected to limit margin expansion and pressure earnings growth, making its discounted valuation less compelling in the near term.

Moreover, Meta continues to face significant regulatory and legal challenges related to privacy, competition, content moderation and youth safety. In August 2026, the company reached an agreement with 52 U.S. attorneys general to resolve litigation related to teen mental health and social media, providing for payments of up to approximately $18.59 billion.

Meanwhile, Reality Labs remains a drag on profitability. The segment reported an operating loss of $4.13 billion in the third quarter, despite continued growth in AI glasses revenues. Meta expects Reality Labs operating losses of $18-$19 billion in 2026, followed by approximately $15 billion in 2027. Although the anticipated reduction is encouraging, persistent losses and uncertain returns from immersive technologies could continue weighing on consolidated profitability.

Story Continues

2026 Earnings Estimate Revisions Negative for META

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the 2026 earnings is pegged at $29.29 per share, down 5% over the past 30 days, suggesting a 24.7% rise from the figure reported in 2025.

Meta Platforms, Inc. Price and Consensus

Meta Platforms, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Meta Platforms, Inc. Quote

The consensus mark for 2026 revenues is pegged at $billion, suggesting 26.7% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

META's AI Integration Boosts User & Advertiser Engagements

Meta continues to benefit from robust digital advertising demand, improving AI-powered recommendation systems and growing engagement across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. Third-quarter 2026 advertising revenues increased 26% year over year to $63.06 billion, supported by a 10% increase in ad impressions and a 14% rise in average price per ad. Family daily active people increased 3% to 3.64 billion, reflecting the strength of its global platform.

Meta's AI-powered advertising systems, including GEM, Andromeda and Meta Generative Recommender, are improving targeting precision and conversion rates. The expansion of generative AI advertising tools and automated campaign optimization capabilities is helping advertisers improve returns on spending. Nearly 10 million advertisers used at least one of Meta's generative AI creative tools during the quarter. Continued improvements in engagement, advertising efficiency and monetization should support revenue growth and reinforce Meta's competitive position.

Meta's investments in its Muse AI ecosystem, including Muse personal agents, Muse Wonder and enterprise AI services, are creating opportunities beyond traditional advertising. More than 10 million people in the United States and Canada adopted Muse personal agents within approximately six weeks of launch, with roughly 25% of registered users engaging daily. Shopping has emerged as a major use case, highlighting opportunities in agent-driven commerce.

Meta plans to monetize Muse through subscriptions, commerce transaction fees, enterprise services and additional business capabilities. The company also sees opportunities to leverage its existing ecosystem of approximately 500 million self-identified small businesses using its family of apps. The company's Meta Enterprise Platform, Muse Code and AI models could generate additional revenue streams as adoption expands. These initiatives strengthen Meta's long-term growth potential, although monetization remains at an early stage.

Conclusion

Meta's discounted valuation, strong digital advertising business and expanding AI capabilities support its long-term growth prospects. Improving ad targeting, rising user engagement and emerging monetization opportunities from the Muse AI ecosystem remain key positives. However, aggressive AI infrastructure spending, rising operating expenses, persistent Reality Labs losses and regulatory uncertainties could continue to pressure profitability and cash flow. Moreover, downward earnings estimate revisions suggest limited near-term upside potential. Although META's attractive valuation offers some downside protection, investors should remain cautious until AI investments translate into sustainable earnings growth and improved margins. Hence, holding META stock appears prudent at current levels.

META currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: 《跌勢美股特報》HOOD,DDOG,BE,FSLR等6檔
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-18 01:06:48 數位內容中心 發佈

Robinhood Markets（HOOD.US）： 成交價67.65美元，下跌6.12%，開盤71.74美元，盤中高點71.88美元，盤中低點67.25美元，均價69.26美元，成交量150.61萬股。

Robinhood近來最明顯的變化，是事件合約已從新產品變成可實際撐住交易收入的重要來源。公司2026年第三季事件合約收入由去年同期2700萬美元增至1.73億美元，幾乎填補加密貨幣交易收入由2.68億美元降至1.2億美元的缺口，也讓事件合約占總營收比重升至12%，高於加密貨幣的8%。同季整體營收年增12%至14.24億美元創單季新高，但淨利仍年減14%至4.76億美元，反映信用卡擴張、新業務投入、投資評價損失與稅負增加正在壓縮獲利。另一個變數是監管，Robinhood已同意在11月2日前停止於俄亥俄州提供新的體育事件合約，顯示這項剛拉動成長的業務，接下來仍要面對州政府限制。Gold會員與融資利息則持續成長，第三季Gold會員增至約520萬人，訂閱收入年增32%至6200萬美元。

Datadog（DDOG.US）： 成交價162.91美元，下跌5.76%，開盤171.2美元，盤中高點172.76美元，盤中低點162.58美元，均價164.91美元，成交量28.15萬股。

Datadog近期可辨識的新訊號，集中在AI相關需求被券商視為比先前更強。Bernstein近期上調Datadog評級，理由正是AI需求增強，代表市場重新把焦點放回企業在雲端監控、可觀測性與相關軟體工具上的支出，而不是單純把它視為一般軟體股。就現有資料來看，近14日內沒有更多公司自行揭露的財報、產品發表、重大客戶採用或財測調整，因此目前最能解釋Datadog營運方向的，仍是外部對需求面的最新判讀。這類訊號的意義在於，若AI工作負載與雲端環境愈複雜，企業對即時監測與效能管理工具的依賴也會提高。只是目前公開資料仍缺乏更具體的公司數字，例如新增客戶、產品收入或管理層指引，因此Datadog現階段的主線偏向需求預期升溫，後續仍要等待公司用實際接單或財報數據進一步確認。

Bloom Energy（BE.US）： 成交價167.97美元，下跌5.25%，開盤181美元，盤中高點181美元，盤中低點163美元，均價170.6美元，成交量171.59萬股。

Bloom Energy最新的主線，已從單一資料中心供電案例擴大到大型跨區域部署。公司11月與NTT DATA達成900MW燃料電池部署協議，將為多個資料中心專案提供場內供電，首批出貨自2027年開始，這也讓Bloom在資料中心的角色更明確轉向主供電，而不只是備援電力。更早前，Bloom與甲骨文的合作也擴大至最多2.8GW，其中初始1.2GW容量已簽約並開始部署。需求面已反映在財務數字上，公司第2季營收約10.7億美元，年增166%，並將2026年全年營收預測上調至39億至42億美元。產品端則推出Power Connect技術，主打把現場電力安裝時間縮短超過40%，並推進800VDC架構，以因應AI資料中心高密度運算用電。只是市場也在檢視其負現金流與利潤率改善是否跟得上營收擴張速度。

First Solar（FSLR.US）： 成交價155.25美元，下跌4.44%，開盤163.62美元，盤中高點163.62美元，盤中低點153.47美元，均價156.81美元，成交量13.73萬股。

First Solar近期沒有出現明確的新訂單、財測調整或重大公司行動，公開訊息更偏向產業位置的再確認。現有資料顯示，公司仍以美國公用事業級太陽能市場為核心，並以碲化鎘薄膜技術區隔主流晶矽路線，這種技術路徑讓它較不依賴中國主導的矽供應鏈，也更直接受惠於美國本土製造補貼政策。市場持續關注的成長支撐，主要來自兩端需求，一是美國政策環境對本土太陽能製造的扶持，二是大型資料中心與科技企業對可追蹤綠電的需求增加。輸入資料並未提供First Solar近14日內新的公司專屬公告，因此目前較難指出營運方向有新的轉折。換言之，First Solar當前仍是依靠既有技術與美國在地製造優勢支撐中期故事，接下來是否出現更明確催化，仍要等待公司對產能、接單或專案進度提出更新。

Super Micro Computer（SMCI.US）： 成交價23.81美元，下跌4.86%，開盤25.21美元，盤中高點25.34美元，盤中低點23.29美元，均價24.27美元，成交量314.84萬股。

Super Micro Computer最近同時出現成長推進與合規壓力兩條主線。一方面，公司宣布H15伺服器平台開始出貨，搭載第六代AMD EPYC9006系列處理器，核心數最多增加33%，PCIe頻寬達2倍，並把產品線從單機伺服器延伸到Helios與Helion等機架級方案，顯示其仍在加快代理式AI與高密度資料中心部署。公司先前公布2027會計年度第一季營收199億美元、年增298%，也反映AI資料中心需求仍強。另一方面，美國司法部正調查與Megaspeed相關交易，釐清是否有關聯實體協助將其產品違規轉運至中國。公司表示Megaspeed從未是其客戶，並已配合美國、台灣與新加坡主管機關調查。也就是說，Super Micro當前不是需求轉弱，而是在AI伺服器出貨擴張的同時，出口合規風險再度成為營運不確定性。

Take-Two（TTWO.US）： 成交價203.05美元，下跌4.88%，開盤216.59美元，盤中高點220美元，盤中低點201.78美元，均價208.39美元，成交量29.52萬股。

Take-Two近來最關鍵的營運變化，仍是《俠盜獵車手VI》預購表現已成為公司未來一年最重要的收入槓桿。管理層表示，GTA6預購量遠高於初期預期，市場資料並顯示截至8月底已產生約490萬份預購。這讓公司即使第二季營收15億美元、低於市場預期，且單季淨預訂額下降18%，仍上調全年營收展望至79.8億至81.8億美元，並重申2027財年淨預訂額80億至82億美元的目標。產品節奏上，GTA6曾兩度延後，最新上市時間為11月19日，因此公司對2027財年將是「歷史性一年」的判斷，幾乎建立在這款作品能否順利推出並延續預購熱度。相較之下，另一款《NBA2K27》自9月上市以來銷量超過400萬套，但表現低於市場預期，凸顯Take-Two目前的營運重心正更集中在GTA新作。

news.Title: Marvell and Intel Are Both Down at Least 50% From Their 2026 Highs. Only 1 Is a Stock I’d Buy.
news.Content:
The AI trade has come under a lot of pressure lately, mostly from investors questioning whether all of the capital expenditures (capex) companies are investing in AI data centers will pay off in sales and earnings down the road.

And two companies that have seen their share prices completely obliterated from their highs back in June are Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC), with both semiconductor stocks down 50% or more from their 2026 highs.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The recent pullback makes it tempting to buy both of these stocks, but just because something is technically cheaper doesn't make it a good deal. Here's why Marvell stock is the far better buy than Intel right now, as the company successfully taps into AI chip demand.

Image source: Getty Images.

Intel's implosion

Intel's share price crash came hard and fast over the past few months, with the biggest drop coming after the company reported its third-quarter results.

Intel has three core businesses: its PC chip business, its data center segment and AI processors, and its foundry business, which makes processors for other companies. Two of those three businesses were a big disappointment in the quarter. Intel's PC chip sales declined 5% to $8.1 billion as soaring memory prices weighed on purchases.

Meanwhile, sales from Intel's foundry business rose 58% to $6.7 billion, but just $411 million of that came from outside customers (the rest was from Intel's own chip production).

Making matters worse, the company issued revenue guidance of about $15.5 billion for the fourth quarter at the midpoint, and earnings per share of $0.25, which were significantly lower than Wall Street's consensus estimates of $17 billion in revenue and $0.43 per share. The company also said its gross margin would decline to 37% from 43%.

But what really shook Intel shareholders' faith may have been the company's $20 billion in capex this year -- a nearly 37% increase from 2025 -- and management saying, "[W]e expect 2027 gross capital spending to be up strongly." Intel investors simply didn't believe the company would make good on all of that spending.

The result of all of this? Intel's shares collapsed 29% the day after it posted the results, marking its worst trading day since the 1970s.

Why Marvell is the better stock to buy

Story Continues

Marvell's recent share price declines deserve some explanation. The most recent significant decline came after reports surfaced that Marvell was in advanced talks to acquire the component maker Lumentum . Marvell will make the $115 billion purchase in an all-stock deal that's expected to close in the first half of 2028.

Marvell's shareholders weren't happy with the decision because it could significantly dilute existing shareholder value. Still, the Lumentum purchase could eventually help Marvell become a key player in the optical connectivity space for AI data centers.

The rest of Marvell's recent declines have mostly come from investors being worried about AI-related overspending. But Marvell's recent quarterly results show that the company continues to benefit from the AI boom.

Marvell's Q2 fiscal 2027 revenue rose 37% from the year-ago quarter to $2.7 billion, and management says sales for the year will increase by 45% to $12 billion. What's more, the company estimates 2031 revenue will be $80 billion -- a 567% jump from fiscal 2027.

The company is also highly profitable, with a non-GAAP (adjusted) Q2 gross margin of nearly 59% and earnings of $0.94 per share. And Marvell's capex spending is negligible as well, reaching just $127 million in Q2.

All of this means Marvell continues to benefit from accelerating AI chip demand, is making substantial profits, and isn't spending as much as some of its peers. That's a recipe for success, and with Marvell stock down about 50% from its recent highs, now could be a good time to start a position.

news.Title: 2027年晶圓、封裝還會旺？　台股3檔一次看
news.Content:
法人發布最新2027年展望研究報告指出，隨著全球AI軍備競賽與雲端服務供應商（CSP）資本支出持續激增，半導體產業價值正加速朝系統級技術協同優化（STCO）與涵蓋先進封裝的Foundry 2.0集中。受生成式AI與邊緣應用擴展帶動，全球半導體市場營收預估將從2025年的8428億美元大幅成長至2027年的2.87兆美元。

全球前五大CSP業者資本支出預估將由2026年的約8000億美元，跨越至2027年的1.17兆美元。隨著摩爾定律推進面臨散熱與漏電流瓶頸，三大製程大廠全面推進GAA與晶背供電網路（BSPDN）。其中台積電（2330）2奈米N2製程首年產出較3奈米高出45%，預估2027年底月產能將達18萬片，次世代A16製程預計於2028年量產並獨家導入超級電軌（SPR）技術。台積電在純晶圓代工市占率預估攀升至77%，預期2027年晶圓報價具備5%至10%上漲空間。競爭對手方面，Intel於18A同步導入RibbonFET與PowerVia，Samsung的2奈米良率改善至50%至60%，並預計2027年推出整合背面供電的SF2Z製程。

先進封裝跨世代 成熟製程現外溢

運算核心與記憶體間的記憶體牆使先進封裝由傳統後段製程晉升為核心系統技術，晶片競爭在電晶體微縮效益放緩下，Chiplet異質整合與先進封裝從2.5D推進至3.5D，成為突破算力與功耗瓶頸的核心關鍵。台積電CoWoS在2027年底月產能估計增至22萬片外，封裝架構亦不再侷限於單一路徑，ASIC與AI晶片擴大導入Chiplet設計，從CoWoS-L與CoWoS-R延伸至SoIC的無凸塊Hybrid Bonding整合。

非台積陣營也齊頭並進，日月光投控（3711）推出FOCoS與解決高TDP供電的3D平台PowerSiP積極擴展市占，Intel亦以EMIB積極爭取CSP客戶訂單。成熟製程方面，雖然消費性電子市場受零組件成本影響，2027年出貨預估仍年減5%至10%，然而AI伺服器周邊對網通、感測器、微控制器（MCU）、電源管理IC（PMIC）及中介層（Interposer）的需求產生顯著外溢效果，帶動2027年成熟製程產能利用率（UTR）維持在90%以上高檔水準。世界先進（5347）在功率半導體結構性缺貨、國際IDM調價循環與新加坡12吋廠加入下，獲利結構將顯著受惠。

news.Title: Microsoft Stock Has Grown Roughly 14-Fold Since Satya Nadella Became CEO in 2014, a 23% Annual Growth Rate. Can That Pace Continue Under Heavy AI Spending?
news.Content:
Satya Nadella took the reins as CEO of Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) in 2014, following Steve Ballmer's 14-year tenure.

Ballmer managed to take Microsoft's revenue from $23 billion in the year he took over to $87 billion by the time he left. Net income climbed 135% in those 14 years. But the stock price ended up in practically the same place it was when he took over, due in part to the government's antitrust suit against Microsoft, the dot-com bubble popping, and the Great Recession in 2008.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

During his tenure, Nadella has focused heavily on the potential of its cloud computing business, which includes Azure and Microsoft 365. Both have produced fantastic results for Microsoft, and its Windows operating system is taking a back seat to those growing businesses these days. Overall, the stock is up more than 14-fold since Nadella took over as CEO, a 23% annualized pace.

But with Microsoft spending huge sums every year to grow its data center infrastructure amid the AI boom, investors are wondering whether it can maintain that torrid pace.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

The biggest question for investors

Microsoft's AI spending has grown considerably over the last few years. Management expects to spend $170 billion on capital expenditures this year, including $50 billion in the final three months of 2026. CFO Amy Hood says that the budget for 2027 will be even bigger.

Those capital expenditures are huge bets, and making them has required Microsoft to raise outside capital. It recently sold $25 billion worth of debt at interest rates ranging from 4.85% to 6.35%. The question investors need to ask is whether Microsoft can produce returns on its invested capital above that cost of capital.

Management has assured investors the answer is a resounding yes.

"We feel good [about] the return on every dollar of capex we're spending. We're confident in that," CFO Amy Hood said on the company's first-quarter earnings call, answering a question about raising capital. "As we continue to improve the efficiencies of our infrastructure, each dollar of capex has the potential to support more revenue and higher returns over time."

However, not all of Microsoft's AI spending will show up as Azure revenue growth. Hood noted that many resources go toward Microsoft's own products and development, which holds back potential Azure revenue growth.

Story Continues

That shows up in its Microsoft 365 sales growth, particularly the growing adoption of Copilot. In its most recent quarterly update, Microsoft said it had 30 million paid Copilot users, but it counts over 450 million Microsoft 365 users.

Both Azure and Microsoft 365 are growing quickly, and that trend is expected to continue for the foreseeable future as capex increases. Azure sales climbed 48% year over year last quarter, accelerating from 43% the quarter before. Microsoft 365 sales increased 17%, accelerating for its commercial segment.

Can Microsoft keep growing its stock price at 23% per year?

Realistically, 23% annualized share price growth is a high bar to meet. Theoretically, the stock should only increase as quickly as management improves earnings per share. In practice, however, that's rarely the case. Investors are willing to pay more or less for each dollar of earnings depending on how optimistic they are about the future.

With the strong growth of Microsoft's cloud computing business and the potential for free cash flow to rise in the years following the big step-up in investment, Microsoft could retire a lot of shares while growing its overall earnings. That should result in very strong earnings-per-share growth, but 23% may be asking a lot over the medium- to long-run. But EPS growth in the high teens, combined with multiple expansion as it proves good returns on its invested capital, could result in the stock climbing by more than 20% per year for the next five years.

Of course, much will depend on market sentiment and on Microsoft's ability to execute its AI development while its Azure customers continue to develop their AI applications and migrate more of their computing needs from on-premises equipment to the cloud. But with Microsoft stock trading at around 26 times forward earnings estimates, there's room for multiple expansion, and it looks like a good opportunity at this price.
