news.Title: KLAC is Overvalued at 9.37X P/S: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
KLA KLAC shares are overvalued, as suggested by the Value Score of F. In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales, KLAC is trading at 9.37X, higher than the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 4.96X. KLAC shares are trading at a premium compared with MKS MKSI, Entegris ENTG and Lam Research LRCX, shares of which are trading at 2.25X, 5.08X and 7.05X, respectively.

KLAC Stock's Valuation

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

So, is the KLA stock a buy, sell or hold at this level? Let's find out.

KLAC Jumps 28% in a Year: What's Driving the Stock?

KLA shares have returned 28% in the trailing 12 months, outperforming the broader sector. Despite its premium valuation, the company's strong position in semiconductor process control, accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, rising demand for advanced packaging solutions and robust cash flow generation support its growth prospects.

The company is benefiting from increasing investments in AI infrastructure, which are driving demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing and process control solutions. The transition toward more complex chip architectures and leading-edge manufacturing nodes is increasing inspection and metrology requirements. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, semiconductor process control revenues increased 29% year over year to $3.75 billion, while wafer inspection revenues surged 37% to $2.11 billion.

KLAC expects the wafer fabrication equipment market, including advanced packaging, to reach the mid-$150 billion range in 2026 and exceed $200 billion in 2027. KLA's growing exposure to advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) represents a significant growth catalyst. Increasing adoption of heterogeneous integration and advanced packaging architectures is creating additional inspection and process control requirements. The company expects advanced packaging process control systems revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in 2026, suggesting more than 70% year-over-year growth, nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced packaging market.

KLA's expanding installed base and increasing semiconductor manufacturing complexity are driving sustained demand for services. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, services revenues increased 14% year over year to $850 million, accounting for approximately 20% of total revenues. Strong demand reflects increasing equipment utilization, longer tool life cycles and customers' growing emphasis on productivity, yield optimization and system availability.

However, KLA continues to face supply chain constraints that could limit its ability to capitalize fully on accelerating semiconductor equipment demand. The company highlighted shortages of critical optical components and other long-lead-time materials, with average equipment lead times extending to approximately 12 months and certain advanced systems requiring even longer. KLA is also facing profitability challenges from persistently elevated memory costs, particularly DRAM used in its systems' image-processing capabilities. The company expects second-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP gross margin of 62.5%, slightly below the 62.7% reported in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and its long-term target range of 63-64%.

The company's share price performance has suffered from these challenges. KLA shares have underperformed MKS, Lam Research and Entegris in a year's time. Shares of MKS, Lam Research and Entegris have returned 45.6%, 47.2% and 92.4%, respectively.

Story Continues

KLAC Stock's Price Performance

KLAC's Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Positive Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues is currently pegged at $4.73 billion, suggesting 43.4% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter. The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at $1.42 per share, up 6% over the past 30 days. The figure suggests 59.6% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

KLA Corporation Price and Consensus

KLA Corporation price-consensus-chart | KLA Corporation Quote

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 revenues is currently pegged at $18.59 billion, suggesting 37% growth from the figure reported in fiscal 2026. The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at $5.73 per share, up 5.3% over the past 30 days. The figure suggests 52.4% growth from the figure reported in fiscal 2026.

Conclusion: Is KLAC Stock a Buy?

Despite its premium valuation, KLA remains an attractive investment proposition, supported by its dominant position in semiconductor process control, accelerating AI infrastructure investments and growing demand for advanced packaging and HBM solutions. The company's expanding services business, robust cash flow generation and improving earnings estimates further strengthen its prospects. Although supply chain constraints and elevated component costs remain near-term challenges, KLA's growing backlog and favorable wafer fabrication equipment spending outlook provide strong revenue visibility. These factors suggest that KLAC's premium valuation is supported by its solid growth potential, making the stock an attractive buy for long-term investors willing to withstand near-term volatility.

KLA currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Workhorse (WKHS) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
news.Content:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Mon, Nov. 16, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Chief Communications Officer - John Williams

Chief Executive Officer - Scott Griffith

Chief Financial Officer - Jody Davis

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Good afternoon. Thank you for joining today's call. Welcome to Workhorse Group's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I will now turn the call over to John Williams, Chief Communications Officer. Mr. Williams, please go ahead.

John Williams: Thank you, operator, and good afternoon, everyone. I would like to welcome all of you to Workhorse's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. On behalf of Workhorse, I would like to thank you for your patience as we had to reschedule this call due to disruptions from last week's global Microsoft outage. Now on to the business at hand. Please note that we have posted our results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, via press release and 8-K and filed our associated quarterly report on Form 10-Q with the SEC. You can find the release and an accompanying presentation in the Investor Relations section of our website. We will be tracking along with the presentation during this call.

Joining me today are Scott Griffith, our Chief Executive Officer; and Jody Davis, our Chief Financial Officer. For today's agenda, please turn to Slide 3. Following my opening remarks, I will hand it over to Scott, who will provide an update on our operational and commercial progress and the strategic priorities we are focused on. He will also provide information on our recently announced partnership with RHAELM for our TerraPod modular data center platform. Jody will then walk us through our financial results for the quarter and our capital position. Scott will then make closing remarks before we open the call for questions. Our cautionary language can be found on Slide 4.

The comments that will be made today include forward-looking statements, which are based on current expectations and projections about future events. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Additional information regarding these risks and uncertainties can be found in today's press release and in our filings with the SEC, including our Forms 10-K and 10-Q. Now I will turn it over to Scott.

Scott Griffith: Thanks, John. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. We've now completed more than 3 full quarters as the new Workhorse. We believe we're tracking well versus the ambitious plans we first announced for the combined company when we closed the Workhorse, Motiv merger 11 months ago. As 2026 comes to a close, we believe the future of Workhorse is becoming more apparent and stronger. Let me start with the current state of play in the commercial electric truck market. As the overall market for electric commercial vehicles continues to evolve, we believe it's becoming even more clear where electric trucks make the most sense.

Story Continues

That's in the depot-based mid- to last mile delivery segment, select municipal uses, including people movers and port and yard uses. There's a reason why. Many of the duty cycles or use cases for these kinds of electric vehicles are the sweet spot for electrification. These are fixed routes, often less than 150 miles per day, where the vehicles return to base each night for cost-effective overnight charging. Fleet managers can assign the right vehicle to the use case, using electric where it makes the most economic sense and using gas or diesel or a hybrid where the route or the use case requires it. Our own experiences as a fleet manager bear this out.

Using full year 2025 actual data, our Stables by Workhorse last mile package delivery business saved $0.43 per mile by using electric trucks based on fuel savings alone. At today's average Ohio gas prices, that advantage increases to around $0.56 per mile. We believe other fleets are experiencing similar cost benefits from switching to electric trucks. As such, we continue to see strong demand from both existing and new commercial fleet customers. This year, we've already announced a follow-on 100 vehicle order from long-time customer Purolator. This is their fourth since the commercial relationship began with Motiv a few years ago.

We've announced a follow-on 200 vehicle order from Gateway Fleet, which offers their customers a simple monthly fee that includes charging and the cost of the vehicle. And we've strengthened our Canadian presence, hiring a country director and just in October, signed a partnership with our first Canadian dealership, Tristan Fleet Management. This is all adding up, and our momentum is building. Our sales pipeline is now 6x larger than it was at the start of 2026. Lastly, the industry overall is seeing a similar trend in the adoption of electric trucks. Amazon is already at scale with their electric last mile vans currently in partnership with Rivian.

FedEx just placed an order for 2,000 electric step vans and they're rolling out charging infrastructure expansion as they execute their FedEx Network 2.0 vision. And in the heavy-duty truck segment, Tesla is now producing and selling electric semis with fleets like Pepsi, Microsoft, IMC Logistics and others. Put it all together, and I think it's safe to say that leading commercial fleet operators are increasingly integrating electric trucks into their fleets with plans to expand to higher and higher levels of electrification as part of long-range planning, especially in the middle and last mile segments.

We remain bullish on the overall market for electric commercial vehicles and in our ability to capture a meaningful share of it in North America. That said, there's still more to do to accelerate large-scale adoption of commercial electric trucks. We need to keep improving our purchase price relative to gas and diesel trucks. We need to work with partners to ease the complexity of adoption and reduce the CapEx needed to install and expand depot and near depot-based charging. And we need to expand financing alternatives as large commercial operators move from smaller scale test fleets to fully integrated electric vehicle truck operations.

Our partnership with Gateway Fleets shows progress on the last 2 points, offering 0 upfront vehicle cost and a single all-inclusive lease that covers both the vehicle and charging. We believe models like this are going to be very well received going forward as they expand into more geographic areas. We're also continuing efforts to develop our modular chassis and next-generation powertrain platforms, which we believe will be a big step forward towards cost reduction and help us to address the relative price of our vehicles.

The modular chassis program will also enable us to grow share in the overall medium-duty commercial truck segment as this platform becomes the basis for developing a wider range of vehicles in our product portfolio. The primary purchasing driver in the $23 billion medium-duty truck market is the annual replacement cycle to keep fleets fresh and manage the average age. We're seeing electric trucks continue to gain share as large commercial fleets replace the annual turnover of aging ICE trucks.

With electric operating costs, often referred to as total cost of ownership, or TCO, continuously proven to be a fraction of the cost of operating ICE-powered trucks, we believe the most efficient way to gain share is to reduce the cost of building electric trucks and pass the savings on to fleet buyers who are ready to make the transition. That is why reducing our bill of materials or BOM, is central to our plans. Our new modular chassis architecture will incorporate highly flexible wheel-based configuration, advanced battery and axle technologies, next-generation software capabilities and an integrated smart power electronics hub.

Our modular chassis will be integrated with our step van products, and we'll also be pairing it with a technically advanced low-cost cab Class 5/6 cab to create a lightweight, high-performance cab chassis platform optimized for efficient upfitting by body builders. This is an important development for us. According to S&P Global data, about 94% of the Class 5/6 medium-duty market is cab chassis and valued at approximately $14.5 billion. We expect the resulting products to deliver increased payload capacity, accelerate time to market for vocational applications and perhaps most importantly, a significantly more competitive price point compared to gas and diesel for fleet customers across a wide range of use cases.

With these developments, we believe Workhorse can potentially capture a much larger percentage of the overall $23 billion market for medium-duty vehicles. We expect our engineering, manufacturing and supply chain efficiency strategies to begin delivering material BOM savings to our current W56 step van products in 2027. We believe the design, engineering and manufacturing changes from our next-generation platform will further reduce BOM costs, and we anticipate bringing the new chassis to market in our 2028 model year. Turning to the launch of our TerraPod modular data center platform.

We're also seizing on what we believe is a historic opportunity to drive new and profitable growth by filling a growing need in the AI infrastructure market with an opportunity that leverages both our engineering capabilities and manufacturing operations. We're not alone in seeing this opportunity. Demand for AI compute is growing faster than traditional data centers can be built and industry leaders, including NVIDIA, are publishing reference designs for modular factory-built AI infrastructure. We believe this new modular design approach will usher in a period of continued growth for AI infrastructure with a new distributed approach that will leverage more locations near existing sources of power.

Industry research from entities, including Grand View and MarketsandMarkets estimates the modular data center market will reach approximately $24 billion in the U.S. and $90 billion globally by 2031. The AI infrastructure industry is adding modular data center designs for several reasons: proximity to power. Power availability is a defining constraint on how fast AI plans can become operational and a smaller footprint can adopt a range of power sources like solar, wind and natural gas to help close the gap. Second is location flexibility and security. Modular units can sit closer to where compute is needed and smaller distributed sites are easier to secure. And then standardization.

For example, NVIDIA's DSX, POD reference design for Vera Rubin AI factories built in modular containers is meant to make construction faster and more uniform. And then lastly, speed. Smaller sites can address permitting issues related to large developments. Sites can also begin computing with modular units as they are installed even while the rest of the site is still being built. These benefits, among others, are why industry leaders are developing reference designs for modular data centers. Our new TerraPod product line is being designed to align with industry reference designs while optimizing the benefits I just outlined. TerraPod systems will be built on a production line rather than a construction site.

They're designed to be sited on deployment-ready foundations, and we believe they can be put into commercial use far faster than conventional facilities. There's growing public discussion about the effect of large-scale data centers on local communities, including electricity rates, concerns about water and land use and excessive noise. We believe the modular approach will address many of these concerns. Here are a few of the benefits provided by modularized AI infrastructure. First, reducing local impact by making deployments smaller and more distributed, modular deployments can reduce concerns about massive structures in proximity to residential areas. Secondly, electricity rates.

By connecting modular data centers directly to existing power sources, modular deployments may help reduce the need to build costly new large-scale power generation. And third, water use. TerraPod is being designed to maximize closed-loop cooling, which when combined with smaller data center footprints is intended to limit water use. Our modular data center line of business is off to a great start. On October 29, we announced what we believe is the start of a foundational partnership with RHAELM, a U.K.-based developer of vertically integrated AI infrastructure to jointly commercialize TerraPod. The partnership will pair our U.S. engineering and manufacturing capabilities with RHAELM's global energy partnerships and AI customer relationships.

We have deliberately structured the partnership in 3 phases: a walk before you run approach designed to streamline and accelerate time to full production while putting our teams together on initial work right now. Phase 1 is to build a reference unit. Under a manufacturing spec unit purchase agreement signed in October, RHAELM will pay Workhorse $10 million for a full-scale TerraPod manufacturing spec unit. We intend for this to be consistent with the standard modular data center blueprint being developed by RHAELM's partners. The unit will serve as a physical reference for equipment fitment, service access and assembly sequence.

This will enable RHAELM, its commercial partners, equipment suppliers and even prospective customers to see, interact and refine the design before committing the capital needed to deliver final prototypes and ultimately begin production. Phase 2 is to sign a supply agreement, which we're targeting for execution by December 31, 2026. We believe this agreement would adopt a structure for milestone-based prepayments toward a first order of 150 TerraPod units and the U.S. right of first refusal, giving Workhorse the opportunity to supply modular AI infrastructure units for all future RHAELM projects in the United States. Phase 3 is to scale production. We currently expect TerraPod production to begin in 2028.

As RHAELM's CEO, Bradd Lewis, put it in our partnership announcement, "As standardization of AI infrastructure continues, turning power into compute moves from the field to the factory. And in partnering with Workhorse, RHAELM now has the manufacturing partner to make this happen." We couldn't agree more at Workhorse. Lastly, merger integration is on track and nearly complete across all priorities, including enterprise systems, office locations, teams and management. The team has done an amazing job of executing on the logistical and technical challenges of integration while increasing deliveries every quarter and starting the process of launching an entirely new product line, all in the space of less than a year.

We remain on track to reach our stated $20 million in run rate synergies by the end of 2026, as Jody will walk you through. We're also preparing a new satellite office in the Bay Area. It will house California engineering, regional sales and service staff and serve as a capabilities demonstration center and as a hub for customer engagement. In summary, I'm pleased with our progress to date, extremely excited about what's yet to come. With that, let me hand it over to Jody for the Q3 financials.

Jody Davis: Thanks, Scott, and good afternoon, everyone. The third quarter reflected revenue growth and cost discipline. Revenue grew 72% from the second quarter. Operating expenses came down 7%, and our synergies are on track to achieve our $20 million target by the end of 2026. I'll walk through the results and the balance sheet and our liquidity. A quick note on comparability. Our third quarter 2026 results reflect the fully combined Workhorse and Motiv operations, while the third quarter of 2025 reflects only Motiv, the accounting acquirer in the reverse merger. Because the sequential comparison of the fully combined operation is more meaningful, my comments today will focus on quarter-over-quarter performance.

The year-over-year comparisons are discussed in our Form 10-Q filed today. Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $6.1 million, an increase of 72% from $3.6 million in the second quarter. We delivered 39 vehicles in the third quarter compared to 26 vehicles in the second quarter. That is our second consecutive quarterly increase, up from 21 vehicles in the first quarter as we ramp W56 production at Union City to meet customer demand. Third quarter deliveries also included 12 older Workhorse vehicles sold from inventory, which generated cash in the quarter. Gross loss in the third quarter was $9.6 million compared to a gross loss of $7.5 million in the second quarter.

The higher loss was driven by higher manufacturing overhead and direct labor costs incurred on the production ramp that incurred in the quarter as well as $1 million of higher costs related to a settlement with a battery supplier. We recorded $0.8 million related to this settlement in the second quarter and $1.8 million in the third quarter. This charge was noncash and reflected in the cost of batteries previously purchased and returned to the supplier as the vehicle model had been discontinued. As fourth quarter volumes increase and we absorb more of Union City's fixed cost base, we expect gross loss per vehicle to improve with further improvement in 2027 as BOM and other cost reduction strategies take effect.

Total operating expenses for the third quarter were $11.1 million, a 7% decrease from $11.9 million in the second quarter. Selling, general and administrative expenses were $7.4 million compared to $7.8 million in the second quarter. Research and development expenses were $3.7 million compared to $4.1 million in the second quarter. Turning to merger synergies. As we have previously communicated, our target is to exit 2026 at a $20 million annualized cost synergy run rate. Based on our third quarter actuals, I am pleased to report that we are on track to exceed our annualized run rate of $20 million. We have realized approximately $13.8 million of synergies through the first 9 months of this year.

The largest contributor is organizational design with combined compensation and benefits running more than 1/3 below the combined premerger operating plans. We are also realizing savings in corporate insurance, sales and marketing and professional services and from bringing contract assembly in-house at Union City. Facility consolidation is still in progress as we expect that benefit to build in 2027 as legacy leases expire. We are reinvesting a portion of these savings in product development, so not all of it shows up as lower reported operating expenses, but we remain on track to exit 2026 at or above our $20 million target. Loss from operations was $20.7 million in the third quarter compared to $19.4 million in the second quarter.

Net interest expense was $1.4 million compared to $0.8 million in the second quarter due to an increase in borrowings in the third quarter to fund working capital and operations. Net loss for the quarter was $21.8 million or $2 per basic and diluted share compared to a net loss of $20.2 million or $1.86 per share in the second quarter. Turning to the balance sheet. As of September 30, we had $4.9 million in cash and cash equivalents plus $0.5 million in restricted cash. We ended the quarter with $40 million outstanding and no availability under our cash flow credit agreement and $18.4 million outstanding and $1.6 million available under our customer order credit agreement.

In October, after quarter end, we borrowed the remaining $1.6 million available under the customer order credit agreement. Also in October, we amended the customer order credit agreement to add $10 million of capacity, bringing the total capacity to $30 million, and we drew down that full amount. We also deferred interest payments on the additional $10 million commitment and extended the deferral on $30 million of the $40 million outstanding under the cash flow credit agreement until after March 31, 2027. As of today, we have $29.8 million in outstanding borrowings and $0.2 million of remaining availability under the customer order credit agreement and $40 million of outstanding borrowings with no remaining availability under the cash flow credit agreement.

Turning to liquidity. We are addressing our capital needs on 3 fronts. First, we are actively pursuing additional capital to fund our growth plan. Second, our controlling stockholder, who is also our lender continues to support the business as reflected in the October amendment that increased our borrowing capacity and deferred our interest into 2027. Third, we are seeking to structure our commercial agreements to help fund working capital, including the $10 million manufacturing spec unit purchase agreement with RHAELM, the milestone-based prepayments contemplated under the supply agreement framework and the milestone payments we are seeking on 2027 vehicle orders.

We are not currently providing specific guidance at this time, but we expect deliveries to increase meaningfully in the fourth quarter as compared to prior quarters, including a record number of W56 step vans as we continue to ramp production at Union City. That ramp supports our previously announced orders from Purolator and Gateway as well as purchase orders from other customers. Looking to 2027, our backlog includes Gateway 200-unit follow-on order with deployments expecting to begin in the second half of 2027. And with that, let me turn it back to Scott.

Scott Griffith: Thanks, Jody. In summary, we have a solid order base and a growing pipeline in our truck business and in modular data centers, a signed agreement for a spec unit and a defined path to the first order. That's why we believe Workhorse is approaching an inflection point. And thanks to our existing manufacturing plant in Union City, we have capacity to build more than 5,000 trucks a year on a single shift, well above today's volumes and the site from which to launch initial production of our TerraPod product line.

We believe we're ready for growth because we have the right pieces in place, an experienced senior leadership team, momentum in our commercial vehicle business, a foundational go-to-market partner in our modular AI infrastructure business with a $10 million manufacturing spec unit agreement in place. Engineering, manufacturing and supply chain efficiency strategies that are showing results with even greater impact expected in 2027 and beyond. And finally, a manufacturing facility already in place and capable of meeting near- and long-term demand. We're also at the epicenter of transformation of 2 major industries, transportation and AI computing. We're designing and manufacturing intelligent industrial machines that are the lifeblood of modern economies.

As we like to say, you can always count on a Workhorse. We believe our evolution into an American industrial technology company is becoming more clear with each day, and it's an exciting time to be at Workhorse. I'm looking forward to a strong finish to 2026 and to sharing our 2027 developments and milestones with you on our next call. We appreciate your continued support, and we look forward to updating you on our progress in the months ahead. Operator, you may now open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question is from Ben Sommers with BTIG.

Benjamin Sommers: So first I wanted to ask on the Canadian market a little bit now that we have our first deal with the Canadian dealer. Just kind of anything to call out there different -- that could potentially be different than the U.S. market? And kind of how do you think about Canada as a market for the longer-term strategy of Workhorse?

Scott Griffith: Ben, good to hear from you. It's Scott. Great question. For obvious reasons, I think it's been talked about even in the press, the larger fleets in Canada are definitely punching above their weight in terms of their adoption of electric vehicles. I mean, overall, that market is probably 12% to 15% of the total size of the market in North America. So it has -- obviously has that limit to it. But it's definitely adopting well in advance of what the U.S. is doing right now. We think our relationship with Purolator, which is very strong. We saw just -- we've got more progress coming, we think, there with additional upside opportunity in the out years.

They're a real leading fleet and other fleets in Canada are really looking at their leadership as, well, geez, if they're working with Workhorse and they've really proven their product line, they've learned all of the ropes you have to learn about infrastructure development and operating a depot that's been electrified. We're really getting benefits from that now, and we're seeing other fleets who are approaching us and/or Purolator, frankly, to learn more about electrifying.

So -- and then the last thing I'd say there's other U.S. fleets who we either do business with or are talking about doing business with in the U.S. that are also operating in Canada, and we find that they're often looking for us to help them electrify in Canada, sometimes even in advance of when they enter in the U.S. because that market is just further along. So it's generally been a real market leader for us, and we expect it to stay that way. And we're going to continue to invest in a presence in the dealer network in Canada.

Benjamin Sommers: Super helpful. And then next, I just wanted to ask a little bit about the AI modular data center business and kind of what stood out as RHAELM as a partner there and kind of how you think about leveraging their existing relationships to kind of scale this business moving forward?

Scott Griffith: Yes. I mean, obviously, RHAELM brings, I think, 2 really strong things for us. One, we have a right of first refusal on any and all RHAELM deliveries in North America or in the U.S., I should say, for modular data systems. So they can go work with other folks, but we get the first right of refusal on all orders that they get. What they bring to the table is offtake agreements, relationships with the very largest cloud builders and AI cloud builders, and they bring capital.

This is obviously a super capital-intensive industry to develop whether they're modular data centers or larger land-based data centers, you need powered land, and in order to get powered land and power companies working, you've got to have a lot of capital and a major balance sheet to do that. That allows us to tap into what I'll call a Tier 1 supply relationship with companies like RHAELM. They've already announced their relationship with the largest power company in Japan, also has a lot of operations here in North America. And they've launched -- they've announced their partnership with Dell and other major hardware and software suppliers in AI. So they bring a really great ecosystem.

They have a whole more of a front end, if you will, on offtake agreements for large offtake deals that they can do, and they have a balance sheet that will continue to develop, we believe, to really support the major project management and product development kinds of opportunities that we'll supply into. So they're almost an ideal partner for us. And they've also seen, even since the last few weeks, there's been a lot of public sentiment about the election results, what's happening in the market, and they're seeing modular data centers as a huge upside opportunity in North America, and we believe we're going to be able to attack that together.

Operator: This will conclude our question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the floor back over to Scott for final comments.

Scott Griffith: Thanks, operator, and thanks to everyone who joined the call today. I do want to reiterate what John said at the beginning about having to postpone today's call from last Thursday. It was a really challenging afternoon with the Microsoft outage. We appreciate your patience, and we're glad you all could make it here today or hear this on record. We're really progressing from a very different company when we first merged in late 2025, early 2026. When I think about where we are now as we get to the last part of 2027, Workhorse is really transitioning from a period of post-merger integration, sort of long-term strategy development, new team formation coming in.

All of that is pretty much behind us now, and we're much more moving toward what we believe will be a growth opportunity defined by operational excellence, market growth, market adoption and strategic partnership development. So we're really excited about the quarters ahead. Today, we talked about progress on this call, increases in vehicle production. We've talked about a really strong Q4 that we believe we're going to deliver a much stronger order backlog. We've had 6x growth in our sales pipeline. We announced our first strategic partner in the modular AI data center or infrastructure business, and we're tracking our synergies on the $20 million target. So there's a lot more than that.

But that's a pretty nice list coming off of about 11 months since the merger. It's really just the beginning. I'm really looking forward to reporting back on our full year results as we turn the calendar in next year. In the meantime, I hope everybody has a healthy and happy holiday season, and we'll see you in 2027. Thanks very much.

Operator: Thank you. This will conclude today's conference. You may disconnect at this time, and thank you for your participation.

news.Title: Walmart and Target make a key customer service blunder
news.Content: I've left Target on multiple occasions because the checkout line seemed absurdly long. I'm not alone in doing that. "More than 3 in 4 shoppers (78%) have left a store empty-handed because of rush-related problems, with the average abandoned shopping trip worth $113 among those who recall their planned spending," according to original consumer research conducted for the Logile 2026 Peak Hour Penalty Report . Some other key findings include: 74% say understaffing during predictable busy periods is a planning failure, not bad luck. 55% have cut back on visits or stopped treating a store as their regular store after repeated bad experiences. 64% say having more checkout lanes open would improve their experience during peak hours. The situation is not unique to Target. I've also witnessed Walmart at peak times with long checkout lines, and I've been frustrated at both retailers trying to find someone to help me on the floor. Staffing issues aren't unique to Walmart and Target. Instead, they're a problem at multiple retailers, which drives customers online, usually to Amazon. Retailers are cutting back on holiday hiring Retailers are expected to add 450,000 jobs in the fourth quarter of 2026, marking one of the smallest seasonal hiring sprees in nearly two decades, according to an analysis of Bureau of Labor Statistics data by Challenger, Gray and Christmas . "If you're doing whatever you can to get somebody to come to your store during the holidays, and you've improperly managed inventory to a point where people can't get what they want, or they can't get somebody to help them because there's not enough people, or the lines are so long it scares them away — that's a huge mistake," customer experience expert and author Shep Hyken told CX Dive . More Target: Best Buy offers a price match policy Target dropped Target makes a big mistake with its latest pricing decision Target has a problem that sends shoppers to Amazon GlobalData Managing Director Neil Saunders made it clear that retailers need to address holiday hiring, but noted that it's not a simple problem to solve. "Holiday hiring numbers need to be treated with a bit of caution, as it's possible to cover the additional workload by allowing existing staff to work more hours — and many elect to do so. That said, understaffing or lack of hours is an issue, and it's one of the major causes of a poor store experience. Ultimately, it can be a false economy — as Target previously found out — because if customers are driven away, then you lose sales and it degrades the bottom line," he posted on RetailWire . Story Continues Neither Target nor Walmart has formally released a national holiday hiring plan. Both chains have handled added hires on a local basis for the past few years, with Walmart leaning on adding hours for existing staff. Amazon offers a smoother shopping experience I order from Amazon nearly every day because it's easy. I only visit a Target or Walmart if I'm looking for something to do or need something right away. I'll walk around a Target drinking a coffee from their Starbucks as entertainment, but even if I find something I want, I'm willing to abandon it if the checkout line looks long. That's part of a bigger problem, according to Headcount CEO Mark Ryski. "To a great extent, many retailers still only allocate more labor hours when sales go up — but the problem is, in the meantime, they're missing sales they could have made every day," he posted on RetailWire. RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino sees it as a penny-wise, pound-foolish strategy. "Retailers spend billions trying to get customers into their stores, and then sometimes make it nearly impossible to find someone who works there," he told TheStreet. That, he noted, plays directly into Amazon's hands. "There's something ridiculous about walking through a massive Walmart or Target looking for an employee, only to realize you could have found the product, ordered it online, and been home by now. At some point, you're not saving money on staffing. You're training customers to shop somewhere else," he added. Related: Costco's $13 billion move challenges its core promise This story was originally published by TheStreet on Nov 17, 2026, where it first appeared in the Retail section. Hotchkis & Wiley , an investment management company, released its third-quarter 2026 investor letter for the "Focused Global Value Fund." The letter can be downloaded here . US quarterly earnings increased over 30% year-over-year, a strong performance amid a non-recessionary recovery, while international earnings grew in the low double digits. This growth occurred despite renewed conflict in the Middle East and the Federal Reserve's first rate hike in over three years. Inflation concerns are rising as the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 3.4% year-over-year. In response, the Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 4.00%. Similarly, the Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) in Europe climbed 3.8%, prompting the European Central Bank to also raise its benchmark rate. Worldwide, long-term bond yields rose, hurting rate-sensitive sectors like utilities and real estate, which underperformed in the MSCI World Value Index. Europe declined 1.7% due to the Middle East conflict, whereas Japan and the US experienced gains. After a strong performance, enthusiasm for AI has cooled, and concerns about financing the AI buildout have risen. Conversely, software companies have thrived, leading the MSCI World Value Index with a 34% return. The quarter showed a notable shift from high beta stocks to strong performance by value and quality stocks, signaling a potential market recalibration towards fundamentals and valuation. The firm believes that its portfolio of financially sound businesses is positioned well to benefit from this trend. Against this backdrop, the portfolio returned 6.42% in the quarter, surpassing the MSCI World Value Index's 3.84% gain. Key contributors included strong stock selection in information technology, primarily from enterprise software, complemented by an overweight in technology and underweight positions in utilities and real estate. news.Title: 《跌勢美股特報》CVLT,NXT,RH,HUBS等10檔
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-18 00:13:35 數位內容中心 發佈

Commvault（CVLT.US）： 成交價137.18美元，下跌6.98%，開盤144.18美元，盤中高點144.18美元，盤中低點135.47美元，均價138.49美元，成交量1.26萬股。

Commvault近期可辨識的公司變化不多，公開資訊主要仍停留在市場對其資料管理與備份復原軟體前景的正面評價，尚未看到新的財報、財測調整、重大產品發布或大型客戶採用進度，足以重新界定營運方向。現有資料僅能確認，Commvault仍被放在勒索攻擊後資料復原與企業備份需求升溫的應用場景中，且在台灣由邁達特列為相關品牌之一，但這屬通路與方案層面的延伸，並非公司新公布的營運成果。對Commvault而言，真正更具解釋力的下一步，仍會是企業備份復原需求是否進一步轉成新訂單、訂閱收入或管理層更新的展望。

Nextpower（NXT.US）： 成交價83.49美元，下跌6.52%，開盤90.61美元，盤中高點92美元，盤中低點81.9美元，均價87.15美元，成交量13.14萬股。

Nextpower正把業務從太陽能追蹤器擴大到逆變器、電氣設備與儲能系統，這是近期最關鍵的營運轉變。2027財年第二季，非追蹤器產品與服務已占單季營收約22%，其中eBOS新接訂單突破1億美元，NX PowerMerge累積訂單規模超過2GW，顯示公司已開始從既有電廠客戶爭取更多設備採購。7月收購Zigor與Apex Power部分業務後，Nextpower也拿下一家大型獨立發電業者1.1GW逆變器框架協議，首批NX Power Conversion系統已交付。另一條新線是儲能，第二季儲能業務營收約1億美元，調整後EBITDA超過2,000萬美元，並包含大型雲端業者AI資料中心用電端專案。雖然新產品壓低獲利率，第二季調整後EBITDA利益率由去年同期24.7%降至22.5%，公司仍將2027財年營收預測由41億至44億美元上修至42億至44.5億美元。

RH（RH.US）： 成交價118.06美元，下跌6.42%，開盤124.33美元，盤中高點125.4美元，盤中低點116.76美元，均價122.8美元，成交量8.27萬股。

RH近14日內未見新的財報、財測修正、重大門市擴張、產品系列發布或資本配置更新，公開資料不足以支持一條新的公司主線。對這類高端家居零售商來說，真正會改變營運判讀的通常是住宅與裝修需求變化、新館開幕節奏、會員銷售表現，或管理層對消費支出的最新說法，但本次資料並未提供這些新增事實。換言之，現階段較難確認RH最近是否在需求回溫、產品組合或獲利結構上出現明確轉折。後續若要重新評估RH，仍需等待公司正式揭露更具體的銷售動能、展店進度或全年展望更新。

HubSpot（HUBS.US）： 成交價218.25美元，下跌5.92%，開盤226.06美元，盤中高點226.06美元，盤中低點215.2美元，均價219.84美元，成交量6.77萬股。

HubSpot最新變化是第三季營收與調整後獲利仍優於預期，但下一季成長預期明顯放慢。公司2026年第三季營收9.476億美元，高於市場預期的9.245億美元，調整後每股盈餘3.81美元，也優於預估的3.28美元，顯示CRM訂閱模式仍具韌性。不過公司對2026年第四季給出的營收指引為9.45億至9.47億美元，低於市場預期的9.649億美元，調整後每股盈餘3.85至3.87美元，也低於預期的4.09美元。這代表市場更在意後續增速，而不只是一季財報是否優於共識。現有資料沒有顯示新的大型客戶合作或併購整合進展，因此短線焦點仍回到既有產品能否維持客戶擴張，以及AI工具商業化是否足以支撐後續收入成長。

Hims & Hers Health（HIMS.US）： 成交價17.54美元，下跌5.48%，開盤18.38美元，盤中高點18.7美元，盤中低點17.25美元，均價17.89美元，成交量141.51萬股。

Hims & Hers Health最近最重要的變化，是減重業務加快由複方GLP-1轉向原廠品牌藥合作。公司11月6日與Eli Lilly合作後，平台可提供Zepbound與Foundayo，自費價格分別為每月299美元起與149美元起，先前也已接入Novo藥品，代表其減重通路模式正由供應短缺時的替代方案，改為整合問診、處方與藥品配送的品牌藥銷售。不過這個轉型也伴隨短期壓力。公司第三季營收8.904億美元，年增49%，但淨損3,300萬美元，訂戶數降至279萬人，低於第二季289萬人，全年營收預測收窄至31.3億至31.5億美元，經調整EBITDA展望也下修。毛利率由74%降至57%，反映品牌藥分銷與國際擴張正改變獲利結構。公司同時推進德國與澳洲品牌整合，顯示海外市場仍是另一條成長線。

Doximity（DOCS.US）： 成交價31.08美元，下跌5.16%，開盤32.37美元，盤中高點32.54美元，盤中低點30.81美元，均價31.43美元，成交量14.52萬股。

Doximity近期主線是把AI功能更深嵌入醫師工作流程，而不只停留在單一工具。現有資料顯示，公司持續以Ask、Scribe、遠距醫療工具與AMiON排班工具整合臨床場景，其中Ask與Scribe被明確列為符合健康保險可攜與責任法案要求的AI工具，且相關AI工具已在數十萬名處方醫師中使用。另一項更具商業化意義的進展，是2027會計年度第2季AI產品滲透擴大，AI Search廣告已被前20大藥廠中的16家採用，AI套件醫療系統客戶也由165家增至超過190家。這代表Doximity的AI不只服務醫師端，也開始對藥廠與醫療系統形成更完整的收入來源，平台重心正持續轉向臨床與商業工作流的雙向整合。

Pegasystems（PEGA.US）： 成交價30.62美元，下跌5.2%，開盤31.53美元，盤中高點31.53美元，盤中低點30.38美元，均價30.72美元，成交量2.78萬股。

Pegasystems近14日沒有新的財報、財測更新、重大客戶簽約或產品發布訊息，現有資料不足以辨識新的營運轉折。對這類企業流程自動化與客戶互動軟體供應商而言，更有解釋力的訊號通常會來自雲端遷移速度、授權轉訂閱進度、AI功能商業化，或大型企業客戶採用節奏，但本次輸入資料沒有提供相關新增事實。這使得市場暫時無法從公司面確認，Pegasystems近期是否在產品組合、收入品質或成長預期上出現新變化。後續若要重新界定其營運方向，仍需等待管理層對接單、雲端ARR或新產品採用的正式更新。

Guidewire Software（GWRE.US）： 成交價146.51美元，下跌5.47%，開盤152.5美元，盤中高點152.54美元，盤中低點145.55美元，均價148.88美元，成交量1.86萬股。

Guidewire近期最核心的變化，不是單季財報失色，而是市場重新下修對其雲端成長速度的期待。公司2026財年第四季非GAAP每股盈餘0.99美元、營收4.11億美元都高於預期，ARR年增19%，訂閱與支援收入成長33%，顯示保險核心系統雲端化仍在推進。不過2027財年的ARR指引雖大致貼近共識，卻低於部分買方原先納入股價的樂觀假設，成為評價修正主因。資料也顯示，雲端ARR已占ARR的84%，年增35%，與Nationwide等大型客戶的長期遷移案仍提供支撐，AI產品ProNavigator與PricingCenter銷售也超出公司原規劃。換言之，Guidewire並非失去成長，而是由高成長定價轉向更看重未來幾年ARR斜率與AI貢獻能否量化。

CAVA（CAVA.US）： 成交價52.12美元，下跌5.49%，開盤54.95美元，盤中高點55.64美元，盤中低點52美元，均價53.38美元，成交量13.88萬股。

CAVA近期最值得注意的變化，是在持續展店同時，擴張成本開始更明顯壓縮利潤。公司2026財年第3季營收3.537億美元，年增22.1%，但GAAP每股盈餘0.11美元與營收都小幅低於市場預期。全年指引中，同店銷售預估由4.5%至6.5%上修至6%至7%，淨新增分店由75至77家上修至76至78家，顯示品牌需求與展店節奏仍穩定；但開店前成本卻由2,200萬至2,250萬美元，大幅上修至2,850萬至2,950萬美元，餐廳層級利潤率區間上限也被下修。另一面，公司已開出第500家分店，版圖進入全美30州與華盛頓特區，並提到新店年化銷售額平均超過300萬美元。也就是說，CAVA的問題不在成長停滯，而在加速擴張需要更高前置投入，短期獲利承壓。

Docusign（DOCU.US）： 成交價75.94美元，下跌4.87%，開盤78美元，盤中高點78.3美元，盤中低點74.72美元，均價75.62美元，成交量8.07萬股。

Docusign近14日內未見新的財報、財測修正、重大併購、產品升級時點或大型企業客戶採用更新，現階段缺乏足以改寫營運方向的公司特定事件。對電子簽署與協議管理軟體公司來說，真正更具解釋力的變化通常會來自企業續約率、平台滲透到更完整協議工作流，或AI與自動化功能開始帶動新一波付費升級，但本次資料並未提供相關新增事實。換言之，市場目前較難僅憑公開資訊判斷Docusign最近是否在需求、產品組合或商業化速度上出現新的拐點。後續仍需等待公司釋出更具體的營運更新，才能重新評估其成長路徑。

news.Title: 《強勢美股特報》CORT,OVV,BURL,RS等10檔
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-18 00:13:38 數位內容中心 發佈

Corcept Therapeutics（CORT.US）： 成交價70.89美元，上漲2.41%，開盤69.3美元，盤中高點71.26美元，盤中低點69.3美元，均價70.3美元，成交量1.55萬股。

Corcept Therapeutics最近可辨識的變化主要來自籌碼結構持續偏多。近一年有1名內部人在公開市場自掏腰包買進約330萬美元股票，均價33.14美元，最近一次為3月17日以33美元買進250萬美元，顯示管理階層曾在更低水位明確加碼。機構端方面，主動型機構於2026年第二季合計持有流通股39.1%，較前一季增加2.4%，持股機構數增加63家至364家，代表專業資金部位仍在擴大。相較之下，10月30日結算的放空餘額占流通股8.3%，回補天數8.1天，但這一波自1月15日起新增空單僅93.9萬股，占流通股約0.9%，資料本身也指出加空幅度不大，參考性相對有限。

Ovintiv（OVV.US）： 成交價64.92美元，上漲1.47%，開盤64.51美元，盤中高點66.1美元，盤中低點64.51美元，均價65.21美元，成交量15.47萬股。

Ovintiv最近的主線是把資本與產量重心更明確集中到高回報油區，並同步提高全年產量目標。公司在2026年第二季把全年石油與凝析油產量指引上調至每日21萬至21.2萬桶，當季日均石油和凝析油產量達20.6萬桶，總產量為61.5萬桶油當量，自由現金流為6.82億美元，每股自由現金流4.46美元。管理層也提到Permian地區運行率已提升至每日12.5萬桶，第三季生產預測約為每日62.8萬桶油當量，其中石油和凝析油約20.8萬桶。另一項更具方向性的動作，是公司近期完成以30億美元出售Anadarko盆地資產，市場關注點轉向出售後資金如何配置，以及是否進一步強化Permian資產效率與減債彈性。管理層並預期下半年股票回購將更頻繁，全年股東回報可望超過60%。

Burlington Stores, Inc.（BURL.US）： 成交價237.84美元，上漲1.14%，開盤234.66美元，盤中高點242.88美元，盤中低點234.01美元，均價238.4美元，成交量3.61萬股。

Burlington最近的關鍵變化不只是銷售成長，而是公司把門市與商品升級計畫推進到更仰賴後端執行的階段。市場討論焦點集中在Store Experience2.0與Merchandising2.0兩項調整，這代表公司正同時改善門市體驗、商品陳列與品類組合，希望把折扣零售的流量優勢轉成更穩定的獲利結構。這套策略能否落地，核心不在前端行銷，而在供應鏈與補貨效率是否能同步升級。若配送中心效率、庫存配置或跨區調度失準，熱門品項缺貨與滯銷品堆積都可能壓縮毛利率，也會削弱新門市體驗的效果。輸入資料同時提到市場先前已反映營收年增11.3%與獲利體質改善的期待，因此後續觀察重點會落在庫存品質、毛利率、同店銷售與物流效率是否一起改善，而非單看營收擴張。

Reliance（RS.US）： 成交價426.69美元，上漲1.33%，開盤422.09美元，盤中高點430.63美元，盤中低點422.09美元，均價425.76美元，成交量1.66萬股。

Reliance近14日內未見更明確的公司特定更新，現有資料也沒有提供新的併購、擴產、財測調整或主要終端需求變化。以目前可用資訊判斷，公開面尚未出現足以重新定義營運方向的新增事件，因此外界暫時難以從公司行動確認鋼鋁加工、庫存策略或接單節奏是否出現明顯轉折。換言之，Reliance近期可辨識的公司變化有限，至少從已提供資料看不出新的基本面催化。

Bruker（BRKR.US）： 成交價61.08美元，上漲0.76%，開盤60.03美元，盤中高點62.08美元，盤中低點60.03美元，均價61.55美元，成交量8.19萬股。

Bruker近14日內同樣缺乏可直接對應公司的新產品發布、財測修正或重大交易資訊。現有爬取內容多與其他公司或產業題材有關，無法作為判斷Bruker近期營運變化的依據。以已提供資料來看，市場尚未取得新的公司事實來確認其分析儀器、生命科學工具或終端研究需求是否有新的強弱變化，因此公開資訊面仍不足以支持更積極的營運敘事。

AAON（AAON.US）： 成交價78.88美元，上漲0.86%，開盤78.87美元，盤中高點80.81美元，盤中低點77美元，均價78.94美元，成交量2.1萬股。

AAON最近最明確的變化，是資料中心冷卻需求已從題材走向接單與產能擴張。公司11月9日公布第三季後，積壓訂單升至18.5億美元，年增40.5%，其中超過80%來自hyperscale客戶，顯示大型雲端客戶已成為接單主力。市場也把焦點放在旗下BASX的擴產進度，相關設施規模被認為可支撐超過20億美元的資料中心營收，代表公司正把原本的商用空調能力更大幅度轉向高容量機房冷卻。為了支應擴張，AAON在11月12日把高級信貸額度擴大並再融資至最高12億美元，另新增供應鏈融資計畫。不過擴張並非沒有代價，資料同時顯示毛利率由26.8%降至24.3%，意味著接單放大與產能建置同步推進下，獲利壓力也已開始反映。

DT Midstream（DTM.US）： 成交價118.38美元，上漲0.42%，開盤117.89美元，盤中高點118.8美元，盤中低點117.89美元，均價118.29美元，成交量1.71萬股。

DT Midstream近14日內沒有對應的公司新聞，提供資料也未見新管線專案、併購、資產出售或財測更新。以目前公開資訊判斷，尚不足以確認公司在天然氣集輸、長程運輸或資本支出規劃上出現新的營運轉折，因此近期可辨識的公司變化相對有限。

Parsons（PSN.US）： 成交價50.25美元，上漲0.53%，開盤49.58美元，盤中高點50.3美元，盤中低點49.58美元，均價50美元，成交量2.28萬股。

Parsons近14日內同樣未見明確的新合約、併購整合、財測修正或政府標案更新。現有資料不足以說明公司近期在國防、基礎建設或資安服務等主要業務線是否出現新的需求變化。就已提供內容來看，公開資訊尚未出現足以改變營運判斷的新增事實，因此近期營運故事仍偏向延續既有方向，而非出現明顯新變化。

Brinker（EAT.US）： 成交價193.82美元，上漲0.28%，開盤191.89美元，盤中高點198.11美元，盤中低點191.66美元，均價195.14美元，成交量4.23萬股。

Brinker最近的變化很明確，就是Chili's持續扮演成長引擎，並讓公司上修全年展望，但品牌結構分化也更明顯。最新資料顯示，公司營收年增7.4%，每股盈餘2.87美元優於預期，同店銷售成長7.5%，其中核心動能幾乎來自Chili's的8.6%成長，反映該品牌在客流、產品組合與執行面仍有競爭力。相對地，Maggiano's同店銷售下滑2.4%，代表集團成長並非全面同步擴張。公司已把2026財年每股盈餘指引上調至13.30至13.90美元，說明管理層對後續表現更有把握。另一項新增事件是Brinker將被納入標普中型股400指數，顯示其市值與規模定位已出現調整，但對營運本身而言，後續關鍵仍是Chili's能否延續強勢，以及Maggiano's是否止跌。

Murphy Oil（MUR.US）： 成交價35.54美元，上漲0.62%，開盤35.53美元，盤中高點36.11美元，盤中低點35.28美元，均價35.56美元，成交量3.89萬股。

Murphy Oil近期沒有新的公司公告可改寫營運方向，現階段最具體的可辨識變化仍停留在先前揭露的產量與現金流組合。已提供資料顯示，公司第二季自由現金流達6.564億美元，天然氣產量增加1.2%，但油氣日產量下降3.5%，代表產出結構出現調整，而不是單純全面增產。同期營收為9.263億美元，每股盈餘1.55美元。除這些既有數據外，近14日內未見新的資產交易、產量指引調整或財測更新，因此市場暫時還沒有新的公司事件可用來重新定義Murphy Oil後續成長節奏。

"We're not going to allow just any outside agent to come inside the company," he said, mainly because it is too risky for clients and for JPMorgan. His concern was that one rogue agent making the same bad call across thousands of accounts at once would be far riskier than a single ...
news.AI_Summary:
• JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon expressed concerns about rogue AI agents accessing customer accounts, leading the bank to restrict outside AI agents, posing a challenge for Meta's Muse AI agent.
• Meta's Muse AI agent, launched in September, achieved 10 million U.S. downloads quickly but has faced access restrictions from Amazon and United Airlines due to security and relationship concerns.
• Meta Platforms (META) stock has experienced volatility, dropping 5% YTD, and is down 20% from its 52-week high after a Q3 report showing negative free cash flow due to increased AI spending.
• Despite AI spending impacts, Meta's valuation appears reasonable with a forward P/E of 21.86x, and the company maintains a solid balance sheet with $32.4B net debt, suggesting potential upside if Muse becomes a revenue-generating business.

ServiceNow（NOW.US）： 成交價94.97美元，下跌4.43%，開盤98美元，盤中高點99美元，盤中低點94.72美元，均價96.45美元，成交量100.63萬股。

ServiceNow近期最明確的變化，是把AI從流程自動化進一步推向資安與合規管理。公司近7天發布Autonomous Security產品組合，整合6項統一安全方案，並新增弱點修復AI Specialist與第2線安全營運中心AI Specialist，讓平台能力從既有工作流程管理延伸到暴露面、身分與事件回應。另一項可量化訊號是，市場文章指出其AI相關年度合約價值在2026年第二季已超過10億美元，代表AI功能不再只是展示性產品，而是開始以合約規模反映商業化進度。公司並強調持續控制監測可輸出SOC2與ISO27001等合規報告，顯示企業採用焦點已不只是模型能力，也包括可稽核的治理與安全證據。

Adobe（ADBE.US）： 成交價236.85美元，下跌3.72%，開盤242.5美元，盤中高點243.32美元，盤中低點235.46美元，均價238.06美元，成交量7.61萬股。

Adobe近14日沒有符合條件的公司新聞，近90天搜尋結果也未提供新的產品定價、企業客戶採用、收購案或全年財測變動。以目前資訊來看，公司最近沒有公開事件足以改變外界對其創意軟體與數位文件業務的既有判斷。這在AI功能快速成為軟體公司敘事核心的環境下尤其明顯，因為若沒有新增的付費轉換、使用量、企業部署或營收指引，外界很難確認Adobe的生成式工具究竟停留在產品強化，還是已開始帶動更直接的商業成果。現階段能確認的不是公司出現新轉折，而是近期缺乏足以重估營運前景的具體新增事實。

Moody's（MCO.US）： 成交價486.54美元，下跌3.9%，開盤499.56美元，盤中高點501.88美元，盤中低點485.82美元，均價493.7美元，成交量7.72萬股。

Moody's近14日查無符合條件的公司新聞，現有資料也沒有新的評級業務動能、分析與數據產品進展，或管理層更新全年展望的內容可供引用。對信用評等與金融資訊服務公司來說，真正能改變營運預期的通常是債券發行環境、訂閱型數據產品成長，或大型客戶與監管層面的變化，但近期公開資訊並未提供這些新增證據。換言之，Moody's目前較像處於營運敘事缺乏新催化的階段，而非已出現明確的公司特定轉折。若後續沒有財報補充、評級活動回升訊號或分析平台採用數據，外界短線仍難以重新校準其成長節奏。

CVS Health（CVS.US）： 成交價85.51美元，下跌3.48%，開盤85.84美元，盤中高點85.84美元，盤中低點84.68美元，均價85.43美元，成交量50.41萬股。

CVS Health已正式宣布將集團拆分為兩家獨立上市公司，這是近期最能改變其營運方向的重大事件，也等同逆轉多年來透過併購打造整合式醫療服務體系的策略。依規劃，拆分預計於2028年上半年完成，屆時CVS Health將保留Aetna保險、Caremark藥品福利管理及其他醫療服務業務，約9,000家實體藥局則獨立為CVS Pharmacy。這項決策發生在公司曾於2006年收購Caremark、2018年再以約780億美元併購Aetna之後，顯示過去的整合模式正面臨重新檢驗。雖然CVS同時公布第三季調整後每股盈餘2.09美元，高於市場預期的1.65美元，並預估2027年每股盈餘至少8.65美元，也高於市場預估的8.53美元，但目前最關鍵的仍是業務拆分本身，而非單季獲利表現。

GoDaddy（GDDY.US）： 成交價107.97美元，下跌3.79%，開盤110.37美元，盤中高點110.94美元，盤中低點107.41美元，均價109.15美元，成交量3.41萬股。

GoDaddy近14日內沒有符合條件的公司新聞，近90天搜尋結果也未見可直接辨識的重大產品發布、併購、客戶簽約或財測異動。以目前可得資訊來看，公司最近沒有新的公開事件足以改寫其營運方向，外界也無法從新聞面確認網站建置、網域、商家工具或訂閱服務是否出現新的加速訊號。對這類中小企業數位服務平台而言，真正重要的通常是新功能帶來的付費轉換、商家採用率提升，或管理層上調年度指引，但近期都未見具體證據。現階段較能確認的事實，是GoDaddy正處於缺乏明確公司催化的階段，短線資訊面相對平淡。

news.Title: Meta Platforms (META) Surges as AI Ranking Models Accelerate U.S. Ad Revenue Growth to 31%
news.Content:
Baron Capital , an investment management company, released its Q3 2026 investor letter for the "Baron Durable Advantage Fund". The letter can be downloaded here . In the quarter, the fund returned 2.2%, in line with the S&P 500's 2.3%. Year to date, the fund is up 5.7%, trailing the index's 12.8%. Notable developments in the quarter included the Federal Reserve raising interest rates and the 10-year Treasury yield reaching its highest since 2002. Middle East developments, inflation, and the AI build-out and AI "bubble" debate influenced market volatility. From a stock-specific perspective, the fund ended the quarter with 13 contributors and 16 detractors, with a focus on high-quality, competitively advantaged businesses. The firm strongly believes in its long-term strategy rooted in identifying and investing in well-managed businesses with competitive advantages. Also, check the fund's top five holdings to see its best picks in 2026.

In its Q3 2026 investor letter, Baron Durable Advantage Fund highlighted that Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ: META ) contributed 1.30% to returns during the quarter. Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META), the parent company of dominant social media platforms, is a multinational technology company that develops products to connect people. On November 16, 2026, Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) closed at $626.41 per share with a market capitalization of $1.60 trillion. Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) pulled back 9.77% over the past month, while remaining up 4.81% over the last 52 weeks.

Baron Durable Advantage Fund stated the following regarding Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

"Shares of Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META), the owner of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads, contributed during the quarter, rising 28.8%. Second quarter results showed the core ad engine is getting stronger: U.S. advertising revenue growth accelerated to 31% as new AI ranking and recommendation models lifted conversions, and Advantage+, its AI-driven ad suite, passed $75 billion in annual revenue run-rate. The bigger catalyst came in September with the launch of Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, which reached No. 1 on the U.S. App Store within days. At its conference, Meta Connect, the company introduced real-time voice, a Mac app with computer use, and commerce partners including Stripe, Shopify, PayPal, Walmart and Best Buy, so that Muse can complete purchases. This further strengthened Meta's positioning and added new potential avenues for monetization, while also improving its contextual understanding of users, which should further advance Meta's ability to match the right ad to the right user at the right time. Meta also brought Muse to its smart glasses and to Charm, a new handheld device. We believe current earnings understate Meta's earnings power as it invests ahead of revenue, and we retain strong conviction that its data, compute, distribution and founder leadership will make it a leader in consumer AI. We also believe AI will remain a tailwind for Meta's core business, helping the company sustain a long duration of growth."

news.Title: Salesforce's Slack Gains Momentum: Can It Lift CRM's Growth Further?
news.Content:
Salesforce, Inc. CRM is gaining fresh growth opportunities from Slack as demand for AI-powered workplace tools increases. Stronger user engagement, rising premium upgrades and deeper integration with Agentforce could help the company generate more business from its existing customer base.

In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Slack recorded its fastest quarterly net new annual order value growth since Salesforce acquired the platform. Slackbot users jumped more than 150% sequentially, reflecting growing interest in AI assistance for workplace tasks. Salesforce also reported that upgrades to premium Slack editions tripled following Slackbot's launch. These trends indicate that AI features are encouraging customers to explore higher-value offerings.

The opportunity extends beyond Slack subscriptions. By integrating Agentforce with Slack, Salesforce can help businesses use AI agents to automate workflows, retrieve information and support employee productivity within their daily work environment. This could make Slack more valuable to enterprise customers while creating additional opportunities to sell Agentforce solutions.

Salesforce's broader AI business is gaining traction. Agentforce's annual recurring revenues (ARR) exceeded $1.5 billion in the second quarter, rising more than 240% year over year. Total second-quarter revenues increased 11% to $11.35 billion, while current remaining performance obligations grew 14% to $33.5 billion in constant currency.

However, Salesforce has not separately disclosed Slack's revenue contribution, making it difficult to measure its direct impact on overall growth. Competition from other workplace platforms also remains a concern. Still, stronger Slack engagement and AI adoption could support customer retention, premium upgrades and cross-selling, helping Salesforce sustain growth over time.

How Do Microsoft and Zoom Challenge CRM's Slack Momentum?

Microsoft Corporation MSFT is a major competitor through Teams, which combines workplace messaging, meetings and collaboration with Microsoft 365 Copilot.

In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenues rose 17% year over year, while paid Microsoft 365 commercial seats grew 5%. Its broad enterprise customer base and AI integration give Teams a strong advantage over Slack.

Zoom Communications, Inc. ZM also competes through Zoom Workplace and its AI Companion features. Its strength lies in combining video meetings, team chat and AI-powered meeting assistance. This integrated offering can appeal to businesses seeking to improve employee productivity without relying on multiple applications.

Story Continues

The company's Enterprise revenues grew 7.8% year over year to $787.5 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. Zoom Communications' competition adds pressure on Salesforce to keep improving Slack's AI capabilities and demonstrate clear value to enterprise customers.

Salesforce's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Salesforce shares have declined 9.4% year to date, while the Zacks Internet – Software industry has risen 1.8%.

Salesforce YTD Price Return Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

From a valuation standpoint, CRM trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 13.29, significantly below the industry's average of 26.90.

Salesforce Forward 12-Month P/E Ratio

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Salesforce's fiscal 2027 earnings implies a year-over-year increase of approximately 33.6%, while estimates for fiscal 2028 indicate a 4.1% decline. Estimates for fiscal 2027 and 2028 earnings have been revised upward in the past 60 days.

news.Title: Applied Materials vs. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
Investors are eyeing the semiconductor boom as artificial intelligence demands faster, more efficient hardware. Choosing between Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) requires weighing equipment leadership against foundry dominance.

Applied Materials provides the specialized equipment and software needed to fabricate advanced semiconductors and displays. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing operates as a pure-play foundry, manufacturing chips for nearly every major tech giant globally. While both sit at the heart of the tech supply chain, they offer different entry points into the silicon market.

The case for Applied Materials

Applied Materials sells the systems, services, and software that enable global manufacturers to build advanced chips and displays. Its materials engineering solutions are essential for creating the complex structures found in modern semiconductors used in everything from smartphones to data centers. Two major customers account for roughly 19% and 15% of its net revenue, respectively, and such customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 25, 2026, revenue reached nearly $34.4 billion, reflecting growth of approximately 21.4% over the previous period. The company generated net income of about $10.1 billion during this time frame. This growth highlights the rising demand for sophisticated production tools as global chipmakers race to increase their manufacturing capacity and transition to smaller, more powerful transistor designs.

As of Applied Materials' October 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio, which compares total debt to shareholders' equity, is approximately 0.3. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, sits at close to 2.3. In the fiscal year ended Oct. 25, 2026, free cash flow was roughly $6.2 billion, providing the company with significant capital to reinvest in research and development.

The case for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing operates as the world's largest dedicated semiconductor foundry, meaning it manufactures chips for other companies rather than designing its own. It serves hundreds of clients worldwide from its facilities in Taiwan, the United States, Japan, and Europe. This dominant position makes it a critical partner for businesses throughout the semiconductor stocks landscape as they transition to advanced nodes.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $150.4 billion, which resulted in net income of close to $76.9 billion. The company saw significant revenue growth of about 36.1%, reflecting its ability to capture a massive share of the high-end chip market. This expansion was largely driven by the surging need for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence accelerators.

Story Continues

As of Taiwan Semi's December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is nearly 2.5, suggesting the company maintains ample liquidity for its complex global operations. Its debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.2, indicating that total liabilities are low compared to shareholder equity. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was approximately $30.2 billion, calculated as cash from operations minus capital expenditures.

Risk profile comparison

Applied Materials faces challenges from the cyclical nature of the equipment market and volatile global demand. The company is particularly exposed to complex geopolitical trade policies and U.S. export controls on shipments to China. These regulatory hurdles led to a $252 million settlement with the U.S. Department of Commerce in February 2026, illustrating the potential for legal and financial penalties.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing operates in a highly capital-intensive industry where it must spend billions annually to maintain its technological lead. While it dominates the foundry market, it faces competition from rivals such as Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) and Samsung (OTC:SSNLF), which are investing heavily in their own fabrication capabilities. Geopolitical tensions surrounding Taiwan also remain a persistent concern for investors evaluating the long-term stability of the supply chain.

Valuation comparison

Applied Materials has a lower forward P/E based on earnings estimates and a lower P/S ratio, which uses sales over the past 12 months.

Metric

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Both Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and Applied Materials reported respectable revenue growth over the past 12 months or so. However, it's worth pointing out that Taiwan Semi has a consistently higher gross profit margin:

TSM Gross Profit Margin data by YCharts

Now, let's check out their historical performance:

TSM data by YCharts

Taiwan Semi has bested Applied Materials' stock over the past decade, but not by much. Shares of both companies have left the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) in the dust. Of course, past performance is no indication of future results.

I've owned shares of Taiwan Semi since 2022, and it's been a solid performer in my portfolio. I don't intend to sell anytime soon. However, just because Taiwan Semi was a good investment in 2022 doesn't mean it's a good investment now . With a market cap of $1.75 trillion, it's reasonable to question how much more the company can grow, especially as the law of large numbers begins to take hold.

As a result, I think Applied Materials looks like a more attractive buy for 2027 and beyond.

news.Title: MRVL vs. AVGO: Which AI Semiconductor Stock Has an Edge Right Now?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology MRVL and Broadcom AVGO are benefiting from the expanding artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market. Broadcom operates as a diversified technology company with strong positions in custom AI accelerators, Ethernet switching and infrastructure software, including VMware, while Marvell Technology is a semiconductor-focused company specializing in custom silicon, optical DSPs and high-speed connectivity.

Broadcom offers greater scale and diversification, while Marvell Technology provides more focused AI infrastructure growth exposure. Let's discuss the differences in growth visibility, profitability, valuation and execution risks to answer the question: Which stock is the better investment right now?

The Case for MRVL Stock

Marvell Technology is benefiting from rising AI infrastructure demand, with custom silicon, interconnect, switching and optics as AI infrastructure momentum speeds up. Marvell Technology's second-quarter fiscal 2027 results extended its AI infrastructure momentum. MRVL's revenues rose 37% year over year to $2.74 billion, with data center up 46% to $2.17 billion and representing 79% of sales.

MRVL's custom silicon strategy continues to benefit from hyperscaler demand for XPU and XPU-attach solutions. MRVL expects custom demand to ramp up in the second half of fiscal 2027 and the business to more than double year over year in fiscal 2028. MRVL's fabless approach allows it to scale advanced silicon without owning manufacturing assets and use funds for R&D and acquisitions.

MRVL is set to acquire Lumentum. This acquisition will add a substantial portfolio of optical and photonic technologies used in AI data centers, cloud infrastructure, telecommunications networks and advanced manufacturing. Lumentum's Optical Circuit Switching, high-speed transceivers and laser components are of the most strategic importance for MRVL, which will make its offerings complete and more valuable.

Marvell Technology's networking business also remains a key beneficiary of rising AI cluster size and bandwidth requirements. In second-quarter fiscal 2027, demand remained elevated for 800G optical DSPs, while 1.6T products ramped up rapidly. Scale-out switching remains on track to more than double in fiscal 2027 as 51.2T products expand across more customers.

Furthermore, MRVL has been reshaping its cost base while prioritizing data center investment. In second-quarter fiscal 2027, non-GAAP operating margin reached 36.6%, up 180 basis points year over year and 160 basis points sequentially, as revenues scaled faster than operating costs. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MRVL's fiscal 2027 bottom line suggests year-over-year growth of 48%. Estimates remained unchanged over the past 30 days.

Story Continues

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Case for AVGO Stock

Broadcom is benefiting from expanding AI infrastructure spending, with custom XPUs and networking driving semiconductor growth while VMware supports infrastructure software. Broadcom also enjoys multiyear engagements with six XPU customers. The broader Ethernet adoption and rising AI deployments provide long-term revenue visibility for AVGO. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, AI semiconductor revenues reached $16.7 billion, which increased 221% year over year and 54% sequentially.

Broadcom's XPU shipments increased more than 3.5 times year over year and represented 73% of AI revenue. Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenues of $21.7 billion in the fourth quarter, up 236% year over year. Management now expects fiscal 2026 AI revenues of $58 billion, up 186% from fiscal 2025. It also expects AI semiconductor revenues to approximately double to $115 billion in fiscal 2027.

In the fiscal third quarter, Broadcom shipped TPU v7 at high volume to Anthropic and Google, began production shipments of TPU v8i to Google, and shipped OpenAI's first-generation Jalapeno accelerator. Management also expects Meta production shipments in the fiscal fourth quarter. Broadcom has a long-term agreement with Google covering future TPU generations and AI networking, while Anthropic and OpenAI have multiyear deployment plans extending through fiscal 2028.

Broadcom's AI opportunity extends beyond accelerators into networking required to scale large compute clusters. In the fiscal third quarter of 2026, AI networking revenues increased more than 2.5 times year over year. However, competition and the attempt to keep products reasonably priced might affect AVGO's margins. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, consolidated non-GAAP gross margin was 75%, down 210 basis points sequentially as AI semiconductors became a larger share of revenue.

Management expects gross margin to decline to approximately 73% in the fiscal fourth quarter from 78% a year earlier, reflecting a higher XPU mix and rising memory content. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AVGO's fiscal 2026 earnings indicates year-over-year growth of 71%. Estimates have been revised downward in the past seven days.

Stock Price Performance and Valuation of MRVL & AVGO

MRVL shares have gained 71% year to date against the decline of 3.7% in AVGO shares.

YTD Performance Chart

AVGO is trading at a forward sales multiple of 8.89X, way below its median of 13.61X. MRVL's forward sales multiple sits at 7.11X, lower than its median of 11.56X over the past year.

Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

Conclusion: MRVL vs. AVGO

Marvell Technology appears better positioned given its accelerating AI data center growth, expanding custom silicon opportunity, strong optical connectivity portfolio and improving operating margins. Its lower forward sales multiple also offers relative valuation appeal. While Broadcom has greater scale, MRVL's focused AI exposure and positive earnings revisions support a stronger investment case currently. MRVL and AVGO carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) each at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Factors to Note for BABA Ahead of Q2 Results

Alibaba's second-quarter fiscal 2027 results are likely to reflect accelerating AI-driven cloud momentum, partly offset by heavy technology investments. In the first quarter, total revenues rose 9% year over year to RMB268.95 billion, while adjusted EBITA fell 30% to RMB27.33 billion.

The AI Cloud and Compute Services segment is expected to have remained the primary growth engine. In the first quarter, segment revenues jumped 45% to RMB48.44 billion, while AI-related product revenues reached RMB12.38 billion, marking a 12th straight quarter of triple-digit growth. Management expected AI and cloud revenue growth to accelerate further in the coming quarters alongside improving profitability as supply ramps, with annualized AI-related product revenues approaching $10 billion in the second quarter. In July, Alibaba previewed Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter model, and released T-Head's SAIL software stack. In September, T-Head unveiled the Zhenwu V900 chip, while Alibaba Cloud announced new regions in Türkiye, Finland and the Netherlands and targeted more than 20 GW of data center capacity by 2032.

The AI Labs and Applications segment is expected to have benefited from paid subscriptions launched on the Qwen App in August, although higher inference costs are likely to have kept losses elevated. The segment's adjusted EBITA loss widened to RMB13.86 billion in the first quarter from RMB3.22 billion a year ago.

Within Alibaba E-commerce Group, quick commerce revenues, which surged 45% to RMB53.30 billion in the first quarter, are expected to have grown on improving unit economics and narrowing losses, though overall profitability is targeted only for fiscal 2029. Roughly 64 million 88VIP members and Qwen-enabled agentic shopping, experienced by 250 million users, are likely to have aided engagement. However, customer management revenues, which declined 7% (up 1% on a like-for-like basis) due to contra revenues from a new business development program, are likely to have remained a drag. AliExpress' operating profitability is expected to have supported International E-commerce. In all others, Amap partnered with Mercedes-Benz in September.

Capex is anticipated to have remained elevated after surging 75% to RMB67.68 billion in the first quarter, resulting in a free cash outflow of RMB44.67 billion. In August, Alibaba raised HK$80 billion through a Hong Kong share placement, earmarking all net proceeds for full-stack AI, which supports its RMB380 billion investment plan but is dilutive. Higher depreciation, inference costs and chip supply constraints are likely to have weighed on margins.

Story Continues

BABA Shares Slump, Valuation Discounted Amid Stiff Competition

BABA shares have plunged 38.2% year to date, underperforming the Zacks Internet – Commerce industry's 3.7% return and the Zacks Retail-Wholesale sector's growth of 5.7%. The decline reflects investor concerns over surging AI-related capex, negative free cash flow, dilution from the Hong Kong share placement and intense domestic e-commerce competition.

BABA's YTD Price Performance

From a valuation standpoint, BABA stock is currently trading at a forward 12-month Price/Earnings ratio of 11.47X compared with the industry's 20.39X. BABA has a Value Score of B. The discount reflects near-term earnings pressure from heavy technology investments.

BABA's Valuation Appears Discounted

Alibaba faces stiff competition from Amazon AMZN, JD.com JD and PDD Holdings PDD. Amazon reported third-quarter 2026 net sales growth of 12% to $201.9 billion, with AWS revenues rising 39.3% on robust AI demand and Bedrock adoption. Amazon also expects AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028. JD.com's second-quarter 2026 revenues fell 2.9%, although JD.com's operating income swung to RMB4.5 billion on narrowing food delivery losses and record retail margins. PDD Holdings' second-quarter 2026 revenues rose 8% to RMB112.4 billion, but PDD Holdings' net income declined 12% on higher ecosystem investments and merchant support. Investors should hold BABA stock as its discounted valuation offers an attractive entry point into accelerating AI cloud monetization.

Investment Thesis

Alibaba is emerging as a full-stack AI leader, with AI Cloud and Compute Services revenues surging 45% to RMB48.44 billion and AI-related product revenues extending triple-digit growth for a 12th straight quarter. Proprietary Zhenwu chips, frontier Qwen models and a targeted expansion beyond 20 GW of data center capacity by 2032 strengthen its competitive moat. Quick commerce is scaling rapidly with narrowing losses, while AliExpress has turned profitable. However, elevated capex, a RMB44.67 billion free cash outflow, rising Qwen inference costs and weak customer management revenues pressure near-term profitability, making disciplined execution on AI monetization critical for sustained earnings recovery.

Conclusion

Alibaba's accelerating AI cloud growth, expanding Qwen ecosystem and narrowing quick commerce losses support long-term prospects. However, elevated capex, negative free cash flow, higher inference costs and weak customer management revenues are likely to have pressured second-quarter fiscal 2027 profitability. Ahead of the results, existing investors should hold the stock, while new investors should wait for a better entry point.

news.Title: How Has Intel (INTC) Evolved Since Its Founder Stepped Down as CEO?
news.Content:
We just published a list of 10 Stocks that Have Survived Major Founder Transitions , and Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC ) ranked 7th on this list.

Several events could test a company, and the exit of its founder is right up there as one of the most notable ones. The analyst community, as well as the broader market, could react disproportionately to the situation, which reflects how closely investors tie a company's prospects to the individual who built it all.

Founders are not just the company executives. They actually lay out the organizational culture, its overall strategy, and often are the face of a company. Many times, market prices in a "founder premium" for the risk-taking ability that professional investment managers might avoid. You also might want to check out our 10 Buy the Dip Stocks Insiders Are Loading Up On After the Recent Market Sell-Off .

When such an individual departs, the market reaction entails a very critical question. It is whether the business's success is attributed to the individual or to the system built around them. The context of these departures carries significance, as some founders leave by choice, while others are forced due to some controversy. Insider Monkey also compiled a list of stocks likely to benefit from interest rate hikes . See the full list here.

Historically, we have seen signs of both warnings and reassurances following such departures. Some businesses lose their way, drifting away without any vision. Others have found that a strong successor, a deep bench, and disciplined processes can carry a business well beyond its creator. Intel is one of the names that managed to survive such a transition and the stock currently has a consensus upside potential of 64.8%.

Gordon Moore, who was the co-founder of Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC), served as the CEO from 1975 till 1987, before passing on the responsibilities to Andy Grove. Under the new leadership, the company experienced a strategic inflection point, pivoting away from its legacy memory chips (DRAM) business toward microprocessors (CPUs). The stock ranked #9 in our list of 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy Now According to Billionaires .

The bull case for Intel centers around the company's strategic turnaround, an uptick in AI-enabled demand, and its pivot into a major U.S.-based semiconductor foundry. It is currently undergoing a strategic shift from its position as a conventional integrated device manufacturer to a contract foundry. Hence, its success going forward rests on securing key external customers for its leading-edge nodes such as the Intel 18A and the upcoming 14A capability.

Story Continues

The prevailing valuation multiples appear demanding for a company still going through a restructuring. The stock trades at a forward earnings multiple of 35.3x, which is on the high side. The topline metrics captivate investor interest, as the price-to-sales ratio sits at 5.1x and the EV/Revenue multiple has clocked in at just 5.5x. These readings highlight how the market is looking well past current earnings and betting more on expected improvements within Intel's foundry business and product suite.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of INTC as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. If you're looking for an extremely undervalued AI stock that also stands to benefit significantly from Trump-era tariffs and the onshoring trend, see our free report on the best short-term AI stock .
