news.Title: Will Content Capex Weigh on Netflix's Free Cash Flow Trajectory?
news.Content:
Netflix 's NFLX elevated content investment is drawing fresh attention to its free cash flow trajectory. In the third quarter of 2026, cash additions to content assets totaled $5.16 billion against content amortization of $4.24 billion, a ratio of about 1.22x. For the first nine months, cash content spend reached $14.93 billion versus amortization of $12.77 billion, or roughly 1.17x, running above the company's full-year expectation of about 1.1x.

Despite the heavier outlay, cash conversion held up. Operating cash flow rose to $3.2 billion from $2.8 billion a year ago, while free cash flow increased 8% to $2.88 billion. Year-to-date free cash flow stands at about $9.5 billion, aided by a strong $5.09 billion in the first quarter, though the second quarter was softer at $1.53 billion. Purchases of property and equipment remained modest at $279 million in the third quarter.

Guidance, however, points to a more measured path. Netflix trimmed its 2026 free cash flow outlook to about $12 billion from $12.5 billion, citing primarily the expected fourth-quarter closing of a real estate transaction, which implies roughly $2.5 billion of fourth-quarter free cash flow. The company expects fourth-quarter revenues of $13.4 billion and a 26% operating margin, including a 120-basis-point hit from headcount reductions, while guiding full-year revenues of $51.1 billion and a 31.5% operating margin. Streaming content obligations climbed to $25.2 billion from $24 billion at 2025-end.

The holiday pipeline is cash-intensive but revenue-supportive. The fourth-quarter slate includes the NFL's Thanksgiving Eve game, a Christmas Day NFL doubleheader, the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua bout, The Diplomat Season 4, Lupin: Part 4 , the final season of Emily in Paris and the film The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth . While front-loaded spending may cap near-term free cash flow expansion, live events and tentpole releases could support engagement and monetization, keeping the longer-term trajectory intact.

How Netflix's Streaming Rivals Balance Spending and Cash Flow

Disney DIS and Amazon AMZN face similar trade-offs. Disney projects fiscal 2026 content spend of about $24 billion, alongside roughly $9 billion of capital expenditures. Disney's fiscal third-quarter free cash flow rose 63% to $3.1 billion, though nine-month free cash flow declined 24% to $5.7 billion amid higher tax payments and sports content spending. Amazon is backing Prime Video with live sports, including Thursday Night Football and NBA on Prime, but its cash profile is driven largely by infrastructure investment. Amazon reported a trailing 12-month free cash outflow of $42.4 billion and still expects 2026 cash capital expenditures of approximately $220 billion.

Story Continues

Netflix shares have plunged 31.2% year to date, underperforming the Zacks Broadcast Radio and Television industry and Zacks Consumer Discretionary sector's decline of 28.5% and 6.7%, respectively.

news.Title: Hims & Hers Bounced Back 9%, But Its Earnings Reveal a Costly Trade-Off
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Hims & Hers Health, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Hims & Hers shares tumbled this week after a Q3 earnings and revenue miss, remaining far below their 2025 highs despite a partial rebound.

The company lowered its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance amid falling subscriber numbers, compressed gross margins, and reduced weight-loss marketing spending.

The FTC lawsuit over alleged privacy and billing violations expanded to include five more states, adding to legal pressure alongside a separate securities class action.

Even a nearly 9% rebound on Wednesday, Nov. 11, couldn't undo a punishing start to the week for Hims & Hers Health (NYSE: HIMS). Shares had already plunged nearly 12% ahead of Monday evening's Q3 earnings report, and disappointing results—a double miss—sent the stock tumbling another 16.6% on Tuesday.

The damage extends well beyond this week's sell-off. Even after Wednesday's recovery, HIMS remains roughly 47% below its July 6 year-to-date high and 71.5% below its all-time high in 2025.

→ D-Wave Quantum Has Long-Term Potential, But Is Now the Time to Buy?

A sustained recovery could prove challenging. With mounting legal troubles, compressed margins, and a reduced full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook, Hims & Hers faces growing pressure to prove its long-term growth strategy can deliver stronger profitability.

Hims & Hers' Earnings Miss Streak Continues

The earnings shortfall was far more pronounced than the revenue miss, which came despite continued strong sales growth.

→ Archer Aviation's FAA Certificate Is a Milestone, But It Isn't the Final One

Earnings per share (EPS) of three cents fell significantly short of the analyst consensus of 6 cents. Revenue, which came in at $890.4 million, was up 49% year over year (YOY) but slightly below the approximately $893 million consensus estimate.

The EPS miss was Hims & Hers' third in a row and fifth in the last six quarters, while the revenue miss was its third in the past four quarters.

→ 3 Stocks Wall Street Likes More Than the Market Does

Subscriber growth was a mixed bag. The company ended Q3 with nearly 2.8 million subscribers, up 13% YOY but approximately 100,000 fewer than in Q2. The figure also fell short of the 3.04 million subscribers expected by analysts.

Management attributed the quarter-over-quarter subscriber decline to reduced U.S. weight-loss marketing and international brand migrations. In his earnings call comments, CEO Andrew Dudum acknowledged that the company is currently in the process of trading "near-term subscriber growth for a stronger position in the years that follow."

Story Continues

Hims & Hers also tightened its full-year revenue outlook to a range of $3.13 billion to $3.15 billion, from a previous range of $3.1 billion to $3.3 billion.

At the same time, management lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA expectations from a range of $275 million to $325 million to $257 million to $277 million. The company attributed the adjustment to planned pricing and marketing investments in the United Kingdom and Germany, along with the timing of deferred weight-loss membership revenue.

For the quarter, Hims & Hers posted a net loss of $33 million, equivalent to a GAAP loss of 14 cents per share, following net income of $15.8 million in Q3 2025. Gross margin was 57%, down from 64% in Q2 and 74% a year earlier, while free cash flow of $26 million marked a notable YOY drop from $79.4 million.

Hims & Hers' Growth Opportunities Come With a Catch

Despite the slight revenue miss, monthly revenue per average subscriber rose 30% YOY to $105.

International expansion provided another bright spot, with revenue outside the United States surging 321% to $233.3 million.

However, approximately $135 million of that revenue came from the company's acquisition of Eucalyptus.

Although management lowered its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance, it had expressed increased confidence in August about achieving its longer-term 2030 targets of at least $6.5 billion in revenue and $1.3 billion in adjusted EBITDA.

Expanded services and products offer another glimmer of hope. According to Dudum, Hims & Hers AI-native infrastructure positions the company "to launch treatments of increasing complexity, including testosterone replacement therapy [in Q4] and our Peptides+ offering later [in November]."

Additionally, Hers-branded revenue is approaching $1 billion in 2026, which supports the company's decision to scale its dermatology and menopause businesses.

Dudum also highlighted the company's ongoing partnerships with Big Pharma mainstays Novo Nordisk (NYSE: NVO) and Eli Lilly (NYSE: LLY), which allow patients to complete virtual consultations, receive prescriptions, and purchase FDA-approved, brand-name GLP-1 weight-loss medications directly through the Hims & Hers telehealth platform.

The Eli Lilly agreement, which was announced on Nov. 6, helps expand access to Zepbound and Foundayo. Previously, patients seeking Lilly's weight-loss medications through Hims & Hers had to leave the platform to complete their purchases through LillyDirect.

The move levels the playing field with Novo Nordisk, which has been offering its weight-loss medications Wegovy and Ozempic on Hims & Hers' platform since March 2026. The agreement also marked a turning point in their relationship, with Novo Nordisk agreeing to dismiss its patent-infringement lawsuit over compounded semaglutide without prejudice.

For Hims & Hers, the availability of both companies' GLP-1 offerings could support long-term revenue growth. However, the shift toward lower-margin branded weight-loss medications, along with international expansion, has contributed to significant gross-margin compression. That leaves investors weighing the potential for a larger customer base against the challenge of restoring stronger profitability.

FTC Lawsuit Expands as Hims & Hers Faces Shareholder Claims

Legal pressure intensified further on Nov. 10, when the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) announced that five additional states—Arizona, Florida, Nebraska, Ohio, and Wisconsin—had joined its lawsuit against Hims & Hers.

The agency originally filed the case on July 29 alongside the Utah Division of Consumer Protection and Los Angeles County Counsel acting on behalf of California. The regulators sued Hims & Hers over alleged privacy and billing violations.

That suit alleges that the company shared consumers' sensitive health information with third-party advertising platforms, including Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) and Snap (NYSE: SNAP), despite promising patient privacy.

According to the complaint, Hims & Hers made subscriptions difficult to cancel, routinely processed initial refill charges 10 days before consumers' selected cadence, and charged for prescriptions almost immediately after consumers submitted an intake form, despite telling them that they could first consult with a medical provider to find a treatment that is "right for them."

Separately, on Sept. 1, a securities class action was filed against Hims & Hers on behalf of shareholders who purchased or acquired the company's stock between Aug. 4, 2025, and July 29, 2026.

The securities lawsuit alleges that Hims & Hers and certain executives violated the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 by making materially misleading statements about the company's business, operations, and prospects and failing to disclose that its privacy and billing practices could expose the company to regulatory scrutiny and potential financial penalties.

Hims & Hers disputes the allegations in the FTC case and has said it intends to vigorously defend itself against the FTC's claims.

Hims & Hers' Next Test: Subscribers and Margins

Wednesday's rebound offered some relief, but the next few quarters will provide a clearer picture of whether Hims & Hers' growth strategy is working.

Management expects reduced U.S. weight-loss marketing to remain a headwind for subscriber growth in Q4, with a renewed marketing push planned for Q1 2027 as the company expands its treatment offerings.

For investors, the key will be whether those efforts can restore subscriber momentum without putting further pressure on gross margins and cash flow.

The expanding FTC lawsuit adds another layer of uncertainty, making sustained improvement in the company's operating performance especially important.

news.Title: Strategy Expands Cloud Subscriptions: Can Software Revenues Recover?
news.Content:
Strategy Inc. MSTR is witnessing strong growth in its cloud subscription business as customers increasingly migrate from traditional on-premises software licenses to cloud-based services. However, declining product license and support revenues continue to weigh on overall software performance, raising questions about the pace of recovery.

In the third quarter of 2026, subscription services revenues surged 49.2% year over year to $68.6 million, accounting for nearly 55% of total software revenues. However, overall software revenues declined 2.6% to $125.4 million. Product license revenues plunged 77.9% to $3.8 million, while product support revenues fell 26.3% to $37.7 million. The growth in subscriptions has not yet fully offset weakness in legacy offerings.

The cloud transition is gaining traction. Subscription revenues increased 53.6% to $190.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, lifting their contribution to total software revenues to 51.2% from 35% a year earlier. Higher cloud adoption, increased usage by existing customers and new contracts are supporting this growth. Subscription gross margin also improved to 72% from 57.4% in the prior-year quarter, reflecting better profitability in the expanding business.

Strategy's cloud-native analytics platform, Strategy Mosaic and generative AI capabilities offer additional opportunities to strengthen customer engagement and drive subscription adoption. However, the company faces challenges from customer attrition, rising cloud infrastructure expenses and competition.

Strategy's software business is making progress toward a recurring-revenue model, but a sustained recovery remains uncertain. Continued subscription growth, improved underlying profitability and the ability to offset declining legacy revenues will be critical to restoring momentum.

How Are Strategy's Competitors Faring?

Microsoft MSFT reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $92.3 billion, up 19% year over year. Microsoft Cloud revenues increased 30% to $63.9 billion, while Azure revenues surged 48%. Its Power BI and Microsoft Fabric platforms offer cloud analytics, data integration and AI-powered capabilities, intensifying competition with Strategy's enterprise software business.

Salesforce CRM reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $11.3 billion, up 11% year over year. Subscription and support revenues rose 12% to $10.8 billion. Agentforce and Data 360 annual recurring revenues came in at $3.9 billion. Its Tableau platforms provide cloud-based analytics and AI-driven insights, challenging Strategy's software offerings.

Story Continues

Strategy's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Strategy shares have gained 26% over the past three months, outperforming the broader industry and the S&P 500 Index.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

In terms of forward 12-month Price/Earnings (P/E), MSTR is currently trading at 5.1X, which is at a discount to the industry average of 13X.

Strategy's estimate revisions reflect a positive trend. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 EPS has been revised upward significantly over the past month. The consensus estimate calls for 14.6% growth year over year.

news.Title: Apple Is Hovering Around an All-Time High Despite the Broader Tech Sell-Off. Will New Products Like the iPhone Duo and HomeView Give Apple Even More Room to Run?
news.Content:
The last few weeks have been difficult for technology investors. This is indicated by the 12% decline of the Vanguard Information Technology ETF since the start of October (as of Nov. 11).

Investors can blame the recent slide on Nvidia shares tanking. In addition to the chief executive officer's latest troubles , the market worries about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Even the smallest shift in sentiment can have a pronounced impact given how important these sorts of businesses are right now.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Amid the turmoil, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) looks like a winner. It's currently trading in record territory, with shares up 31% this year. The $5.2 trillion market capitalization easily makes it the world's most valuable company. It makes sense if investors view this as more of a consumer staples stock rather than a pure tech stock.

The business continues to operate as it always has, with fresh product releases a cornerstone of the strategy. The iPhone Duo and HomeView are the most notable launches. Will these innovations give Apple shares more room to run?

Skipping the arms race

The stock's recent strength underscores its unique AI strategy. This business has not participated in the extraordinary infrastructure boom that's seeing its tech peers spend hundreds of billions of dollars on data centers, often raising external capital to do so. Capital outlays of this size naturally increase the financial risk investors must deal with.

And this puts the AI trade on fragile ground. The market wants rapid growth to continue for hyperscaler cloud platforms and the leading AI labs. No one can accurately predict what the industry will look like in two to three years, which is the problem that introduces immense uncertainty.

Apple is standing by itself. It collected $136 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2026 (ended Sept. 26), thanks to just $9 billion in capital expenditures. Investors have always appreciated the financial strength this business operates with.

Even during a major technological wave that encourages heavy spending, its profitability has held up. Management's discipline is why certain Apple bulls might be comfortable calling this a safe-haven stock .

Own it for quality, not for huge returns

A premium brand defined by pricing power, customer loyalty, and an unmatched ecosystem make Apple an elite company. And the constant focus on innovation keeps consumers interested. But investors face a trade-off. In exchange for owning such a high-quality business, you give up the potential to capture outsize returns.

Story Continues

The valuation could be a headwind. Shares are at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 36.4, which doesn't present investors with a margin of safety. You essentially have to believe the market will continue to assign a high multiple to the stock.

Growth will also naturally slow. According to sell-side analyst estimates, Apple's revenue and earnings per share are expected to increase by just 27% and 31%, respectively, over the next three years.

This is accounting for the impact new products will have. The iPhone Duo immediately saw incredible demand. But the consensus view is that it will only represent 7% of iPhone revenue this fiscal year.

And it's too early to draw any conclusions about HomeView. However, this will have a tiny near-term financial impact even if tens of millions of units are sold.

These could end up being extremely successful products. The issue is that Apple is so massive, with fiscal 2026 net sales coming in at $479 billion. It's virtually impossible to move the financial needle at this size.

This isn't to say that the stock can't continue its ascent. It's just important that investors set the right expectations if they do choose to buy Apple.

news.Title: Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.

Shares of this chipmaker have returned -31.2% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -2.4% change. The Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, to which Marvell belongs, has lost 14.4% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Marvell is expected to post earnings of $1.10 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +44.7%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -0.2%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $4.21 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +48.2%. This estimate has changed -0.2% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $7.42 indicates a change of +76.2% from what Marvell is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.8%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Marvell.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Projected Revenue Growth

Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.

For Marvell, the consensus sales estimate for the current quarter of $3.16 billion indicates a year-over-year change of +52.2%. For the current and next fiscal years, $12.06 billion and $19.89 billion estimates indicate +47.1% and +65% changes, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Marvell reported revenues of $2.74 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +36.5%. EPS of $0.94 for the same period compares with $0.67 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.71 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +1.03%. The EPS surprise was +1.08%.

Over the last four quarters, Marvell surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

Without considering a stock's valuation, no investment decision can be efficient. In predicting a stock's future price performance, it's crucial to determine whether its current price correctly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Marvell is graded F on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Conclusion

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Marvell. However, its Zacks Rank #2 does suggest that it may outperform the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: Onto Innovation's Q3 Cash Flow Hits $79M: Is Momentum Sustainable?
news.Content:
Onto Innovation ONTO delivered improved cash generation in the third quarter of 2026, supported by strong semiconductor equipment demand and operational efficiency.

The company generated approximately $79 million in operating cash flow, up from roughly $62 million in the preceding quarter. The company ended September 2026 with $1.25 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, which includes free cash flow generated in the quarter. However, it is lower than $1.88 billion reported at June-end, mainly due to the $720 million payment made to acquire a 27% stake in Rigaku, which was completed in August.

The company's strong financial performance underscores its cash-generating potential. Third-quarter revenues surged 88% year over year and 19% sequentially to $410 million. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 60 basis points sequentially to 57.6%, while non-GAAP operating margin reached 32.6%. Management attributed improving profitability to higher productivity, the extended factory model and better operating leverage.

Looking forward, strong demand from advanced packaging and advanced nodes should support top-line expansion. Onto Innovation's backlog increased to more than $1.3 billion during the third quarter. Management cited strong customer demand and visibility into investment plans extending multiple years. It expects full-year 2026 revenue growth to exceed 45% year over year and anticipates sequential revenue growth through at least the first half of 2027.

Onto Innovation Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Onto Innovation Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Onto Innovation Inc. Quote

The company expects fourth-quarter revenues between $430 million and $450 million, with non-GAAP operating margin in the range of 33.5%-34.5%.

However, cash flow sustainability warrants attention. Operating cash flow for the first nine months of 2026 declined to $166.6 million from $233.3 million a year earlier, reflecting higher inventories and the timing of customer collections.

Moreover, cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities increased to $1.25 billion at September-end from $639.6 million as of Jan. 3, 2026, supported mainly by cash provided by financing activities. In May, ONTO issued $1.5 billion of 0% convertible notes due in 2031. The financing generated about $1.2 billion of net cash after nearly $300 million worth of share repurchases, capped calls and transaction costs.

Balance Sheet Snapshot for Peers

KLA Corporation KLAC remains a formidable competitor. The company generated free cash flow of $1.34 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, supported by operating cash flow of $1.53 billion. Revenues jumped 29% year over year and 13% sequentially to $4.14 billion, driven by AI-related investments and increasing process-control intensity across edge devices and advanced packaging. KLA ended the quarter with $4.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities against $5.95 billion in debt.

Story Continues

Looking ahead, management expects December-quarter revenues of $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million.

Nova Ltd. NVMI generated $132 million in free cash flow in the third quarter of 2026, bringing the nine-month total to approximately $206 million. Revenues increased 28% year over year and 13% sequentially to $287.8 million, supported by robust demand for memory and advanced packaging solutions. Nova exited the quarter with approximately $1.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents, bank deposits and marketable securities.

For the fourth quarter, management projects revenues between $305 million and $315 million. Growing adoption of its Nova WMC platform across logic and HBM applications, alongside continued investments in advanced metrology solutions, is strengthening the company's competitive position.

ONTO Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

ONTO's shares have lost 18.4% in the past month, outperforming the Zacks Nanotechnology industry's decline of 24.7%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

On a forward price-to-earnings basis, ONTO's shares trade at 19.16X, higher than the industry's 3.34X.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ONTO's earnings has moved up for both 2026 and 2027 over the past 60 days.

Onto Innovation currently holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Alphabet's Cloud Business Doubled, but the Stock Plunged. Here's What a $5,000 Investment Could Be Worth by 2030.
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) reported third-quarter earnings on Oct. 28. Since then, the stock sold off and hasn't recovered. It was down more than 10% since reporting earnings, which is no small amount considering that Alphabet is one of the world's largest companies.

However, Alphabet's sell-off was more focused on its spending rather than its growth. I think this is a very short-sighted view by the market, and it's why Alphabet stock should be considered a strong buy right now.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

If the company keeps up the pace, a $5,000 investment could be worth $11,000 by 2030. Here's how.

Google Cloud is the highlight of the company

Alphabet's business was built on Google Search. However, a new segment is starting to lead the company: cloud computing . Google Cloud is one of the largest cloud computing firms in the world and could start closing the gap, due to how fast it's growing.

In Q3, its revenue rose 103% year over year to $30.7 billion. Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the industry leader and generated $46 billion in Q3, growing at 39%. So, Google Cloud has a chance to start catching up to Amazon over the next year, but not all of its revenue is recurring.

For the most part, cloud computing revenue can be recognized as recurring, as clients pay for usage, which is generally fairly recurring revenue. However, Alphabet is starting to sell its proprietary artificial intelligence computing chips to certain firms, which is boosting its revenue.

Unfortunately, Alphabet doesn't provide investors with Tensor Processing Unit sales figures, so it's impossible to parse how much revenue is from chip sales and how much is from a more recurring revenue stream. The best clue investors have is that Alphabet stated that cloud revenue makes up the "vast majority" of revenue and that the growth rate, excluding TPU sales, was "incredibly strong." However, 2027 will include far more chip sales, which could affect the 2027 revenue guidance investors may see during Q4.

However, the legacy business wasn't the greatest for Alphabet. Google Search had an OK quarter, with revenue growing 12% year over year. YouTube didn't fare any better, with revenue rising 9% year over year. But Alphabet's total revenue rose at a 25% year-over-year rate, thanks to the strength of Google Cloud, which now makes up nearly a quarter of its total business.

Story Continues

But where will that take the stock by 2030? Let's take a look.

Google Cloud will take the company to new heights

Many in the cloud computing industry project several years of strong growth driven by rising AI workloads . Google Cloud's peers are growing at a 40% rate, but with Google Cloud's TPUs becoming a popular alternative to GPUs for running workloads, I think it will grow faster than its peers, growing at a 50% rate. This will help boost Alphabet's overall growth rate, and a 20% companywide growth rate from now until 2030 isn't out of the question. If Alphabet does that, it could have trailing 12-month revenue totals of just over $1 trillion.

GOOG Revenue (TTM) data by YCharts

Trillion-dollar revenue companies are quickly approaching, and Alphabet will be among the first to reach this mark. If it can deliver a 30% profit margin and trade for 25 times earnings, that would value the stock at $7.7 trillion. Alphabet currently has a $3.5 trillion valuation, so this would transform a $5,000 investment today into about $11,000.

That's a great, market-beating investment, and investors should use today's sale price as a smart buying opportunity for Alphabet stock.

news.Title: Netlist's Q3 Sales Surge 149%: Can the Momentum Continue?
news.Content:
Netlist, Inc. NLST delivered robust third-quarter 2026 results, with net sales increasing 149% year over year to $105.1 million. The quarterly performance was supported by strong demand for AI and data center memory products and the commencement of licensing revenues under its Samsung agreement.

Netlist's third-quarter product sales increased 43% year over year to $60.2 million, reflecting healthy demand from AI and data center customers. The company also recognized $44.9 million in licensing revenues under its Samsung agreement, significantly strengthening the overall revenue base.

Expanding licensing portfolio and favorable market conditions are likely to sustain Netlist's growth momentum going forward.

Looking ahead, the company expects fourth-quarter 2026 product sales to increase substantially from the third quarter, supported by rising demand for its products and initial Samsung product sales under the product supply agreement.

Netlist, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Netlist, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Netlist, Inc. Quote

Meanwhile, its recently concluded Micron agreement provides another growth catalyst. Beginning in the fourth quarter, Netlist expects combined quarterly licensing revenues of approximately $73 million from Samsung and Micron, translating into an annualized run rate of $292 million.

Netlist remains focused on portfolio expansion to boost its presence in the AI memory market. The company recently announced next-generation LIGHTNING Ultra-Low Latency DDR5 RDIMMs for Agentic AI workstations and servers. The DDR5-6000 and DDR5-6400 products are designed to boost responsiveness in memory-sensitive AI and enterprise workloads.

The new products target agentic AI workstations and servers, multi-agent systems, retrieval-augmented generation, large language models and vector databases. Applications also extend to high-frequency trading, scientific computing and electronic design automation, cloud infrastructure and data analytics.

While recurring licensing revenues provide a relatively predictable foundation, continued expansion in the product business will determine whether Netlist can maintain its impressive growth trajectory.

Revenue Performance for Peers

Netlist operates in a highly competitive memory market alongside established players, including SK hynix SKHY and Rambus RMBS.

Rambus' third-quarter 2026 revenues of $218.3 million jumped 22% year over year, buoyed by demand for advanced memory solutions for next-generation AI and data center infrastructure. Product revenues increased 22% to $114.3 million.

Story Continues

For the fourth quarter, Rambus expects revenues between $227 million and $233 million, with product revenues projected at $127-$133 million, implying 34% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. Increasing AI infrastructure investments and expanding adoption of DDR5 solutions are expected to sustain growth. Management anticipates strengthening demand heading into 2027.

South Korea-based SK hynix has a strong presence across DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory ("HBM") markets. Third-quarter 2026 revenues were KRW 104.6 trillion, soaring 328% year over year and 32% sequentially. Growth was driven by rising DRAM and NAND prices, and robust demand trends.

Management highlighted that the mass production and shipments of HBM4 began in the third quarter, while shipments of server DDR5 increased more than 40% sequentially. For the fourth quarter, management expects DRAM shipment volume to increase a mid-20% sequentially, while NAND bit shipments are projected to rise by a mid-single-digit percentage.

news.Title: 2 Memory Stocks to Buy and Hold Through 2030
news.Content:
Memory stocks have had quite the year in 2026. Two of the best performers are Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) and Micron (NASDAQ: MU), which are each among the top five best-performing stocks in the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) this year.

Sandisk holds second place, rising around 270%, while Micron has risen about 150%. However, I think both of these stocks are due for more over the next few years, and all investors have to do is listen to what they're saying.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

I think these two will be great stocks to buy and hold over the next few years, and could deliver monster returns.

Both stocks are incredibly cheap versus the broader market

Memory chips are required for many devices to function. Long-term data storage utilizes NAND memory, such as in solid-state drives (SSDs). Computing units need DRAM memory to function, and these are being deployed heavily in data centers for computing power.

While memory chips are necessary, there isn't much to differentiate one memory chip from another. With no competitive advantage, memory chips basically became a commodity. As a result, pricing depends heavily on supply and demand. This makes memory chips a cyclical industry, and investors have historically given companies in these fields deep discounts to avoid losing vast sums of money when the cycle turns.

That's what the market is betting will happen for Micron and Sandisk. With the AI build-out in full force and consuming all available memory, demand for chip production capacity for their products has never been higher. With production capacity sold out, prices have also skyrocketed. This has led to ludicrous growth rates for each company, but the market isn't valuing them fully because of their cyclical nature.

MU PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

For reference, the S&P 500 trades at 19 times forward earnings, so if both stocks just had a market-average valuation, they would rise nearly 5 times in value. But because the market is betting on a downturn, they're cheap.

The memory chip industry is being reshaped

Both of these companies are taking steps to reduce the cyclical nature of their businesses. Instead of selling products on the open market, both are now entering into long-term agreements with their clients. Sandisk calls this its "New Business Model" (NBM), and a large chunk of its revenue is coming from these agreements. Micron is doing the same thing and has locked in approximately 35% of revenue through 2030 with these types of contracts.

Story Continues

Why is this a big deal? It raises the floor for the companies. Instead of dealing with a significant pricing decline as demand falls when the AI build-out ends, there are floor pricing levels with their clients that keep the business running well. So, Micron and Sandisk may not see the massive pricing highs they're seeing now ever again, but they won't experience the lows that result in the stocks not being highly valued. This means the market should reprice the stock accordingly, which could lead to massive upside in the near future.

Furthermore, the industry has been sold out for many years, and Micron told investors that market conditions in 2027 and 2028 will likely be tighter than in 2026. The reality is that the memory space will be tied up for multiple years, likely through 2030, and these two stocks will make for excellent investments during that time. There's a good chance memory stocks will become a hot commodity sometime in the near future, and that makes now the perfect time to load up on them.

news.Title: As October Revenue Surges, Wall Street Is Still Bullish on Taiwan Semi Stock
news.Content:
Unprecedented global demand for advanced artificial intelligence hardware continues to drive historic revenue expansion across leading semiconductor foundries. As tech hyperscalers aggressively expand data center capacity, cutting-edge wafer production and next-generation packaging capabilities remain fully booked, insulating top-tier chip manufacturers from broader consumer electronics demand fluctuations.

Underlining this booming chip demand, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) reported an October revenue surge of nearly 60% year-over-year.

About Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing — widely known as TSMC — is the world's leading dedicated semiconductor foundry. Headquartered in Taiwan, the company manufactures advanced chips for global technology leaders, including Nvidia (NVDA) and Apple (AAPL). Its cutting-edge 2-nanometer, 3-nanometer, and advanced packaging technologies make it a key player in the artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor industries.

TSM Stock Delivers Strong 2026 Returns

TSMC stock has delivered strong gains in 2026, supported by accelerating demand for artificial intelligence chips, advanced semiconductor manufacturing, and high-performance computing infrastructure. The company's U.S.-listed American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) closed at approximately $396.48 on Nov. 10, giving the stock a year-to-date price gain of around 30.5% from its 2025 closing level. However, shares have experienced volatility, retreating from their 52-week high of approximately $487.47, as investors reassessed technology valuations and the sustainability of AI-related spending.

TSMC Quarterly Results

TSMC reported strong third-quarter 2026 financial results, driven by sustained demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing and AI-related chips. Revenue reached NT$1.494 trillion (approximately $46.72 billion), increasing 50.9% year over year and exceeding the LSEG analyst estimate of approximately NT$1.46 trillion. Diluted earnings per share came in at NT$29.43, compared with the analyst consensus of NT$28.89, while net income climbed 68.7% year over year to NT$763.06 billion. The results reflected continued momentum across the global semiconductor industry, particularly in AI infrastructure and high-performance computing.

Story Continues

The company maintained strong profitability, with gross margin reaching 66.4%, operating margin at 58.7%, and net profit margin at 51.1%. Gross profit increased 68.6% year over year to NT$992.38 billion, while operating income rose 75% to NT$876.45 billion. Advanced technologies, including 2-nanometer, 3-nanometer, 5-nanometer, and 7-nanometer processes, accounted for 79% of total wafer revenue. Notably, 3-nanometer technology contributed 33%, while the newly ramping 2-nanometer process represented 8%.

Looking ahead, TSMC management expects strong demand for leading-edge process technologies to support its fourth-quarter 2026 performance, particularly as production of its 2-nanometer technology ramps up. The company forecasts fourth-quarter revenue between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion, with gross margin projected at 65%-67% and operating margin at 56.5%-58.5%.

TSMC Revenue Jumps 60%

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing reported a 59.7% year-over-year increase in October 2026 revenue to NT$586.89 billion ($18.4 billion), highlighting robust demand for advanced semiconductors used in artificial intelligence applications.

The world's largest contract chipmaker generated NT$4.49 trillion in revenue during the first 10 months of 2026, marking a 43.3% increase from the same period last year. Analysts expect revenue growth to accelerate to approximately 63% in the final quarter, following TSMC's September-quarter revenue of $46.72 billion, which exceeded the $45.7 billion analyst estimate.

TSMC shares listed in Taiwan rose 2.2% ahead of the revenue announcement. As a major supplier to Nvidia and Apple, TSMC remains well positioned to benefit from rising AI infrastructure investment and demand for advanced chip manufacturing.

Should You Buy TSM?

TSMC's October revenue surge of nearly 60% highlights strong demand for AI chips and reinforces its position as a leading semiconductor manufacturer. Continued investment in AI infrastructure could provide further growth opportunities, although market volatility and semiconductor industry risks remain important considerations. Wall Street maintains a "Strong Buy" consensus on TSM, with an average price target of $536.64, suggesting 35.5% potential upside from its current market price. Among 19 analyst ratings, 16 are "Strong Buy," two are "Moderate Buy," and one is "Hold," reflecting broadly positive sentiment toward TSMC's growth prospects.

news.Title: Tesla to Wind Down Cybertruck: Can Cybercab Justify the Shift?
news.Content:
Tesla TSLA is making room for a different future at its Gigafactory Texas plant. The company is expected to bring Cybertruck production to a close in fall 2027, with the factory space eventually being used to build Cybercab, its driverless vehicle. The move comes as the electric pickup struggled to attract mass-market buyers and fell short of the sales volumes Elon Musk once envisioned.

This is not simply a decision to stop making an underperforming model. It reflects Tesla's growing preference for autonomy and robotics over some parts of its traditional vehicle business. The bigger question is whether these newer ambitions can generate enough business for the company.

Cybertruck Struggles to Meet Its Sales Ambitions

When Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck, Musk set an ambitious target of selling 250,000 units annually. Its unconventional design attracted plenty of attention, but the initial excitement did not translate into sustained demand.

Per CNBC, Cox Automotive estimated that Tesla sold just 20,237 Cybertrucks in the United States in 2025, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Several recalls have added to the model's challenges, while its high price has limited its appeal to a wider pool of buyers.

Production capacity further highlights the mismatch. Tesla had installed capacity to produce more than 125,000 Cybertrucks annually, but the vehicle was selling at a pace of roughly 30,000 units a year before the wind-down announcement last Friday. That leaves considerable manufacturing capacity underutilized.

Tesla has now stopped accepting orders for the Premium AWD version, leaving the Cyberbeast as the only available configuration. Its price has increased by $7,500 to $109,990. Buyers placing orders now are being given delivery estimates between March and June 2027. Musk has said production will continue until the end of summer 2027 to work through the remaining backlog.

An interesting part of the sales story is SpaceX SPCX. Musk's aerospace, communications and AI company purchased $131 million worth of Cybertrucks last year at Tesla's suggested retail price, according to a SpaceX financial filing. While these purchases contributed to demand, they also raise questions about how much of the Cybertruck's sales momentum came from buyers outside the broader retail market.

Tesla is not alone in discovering how difficult it is to make electric pickups profitable. Ford F, which operates in the highly profitable U.S. pickup market, has also struggled to make its electric F-150 Lightning commercially viable and has decided to discontinue the model. Ford continues to report losses in its EV business but is working on a more affordable electric pickup. This highlights the difficulty of building a profitable electric truck business, even for established automakers with strong pickup franchises.

Story Continues

Cybercab and Optimus Become Tesla's Priorities

The factory space freed up by the Cybertruck's departure is expected to support Cybercab manufacturing. Cybercab is designed as a two-seat, fully autonomous vehicle without a steering wheel or pedals.

Musk sees Cybercab as central to Tesla's transportation-as-a-service strategy, in which autonomous vehicles could generate revenues by providing paid rides rather than relying solely on individual vehicle sales. If successful, this model could create recurring revenue opportunities and change how Tesla generates returns from its vehicle fleet.

But the economics are still a big question mark. Tesla must show that its technology can handle driverless operations reliably, win the necessary regulatory permissions and attract enough customers to support a commercially viable service. Manufacturing Cybercab at scale will matter only if the company can put those vehicles to productive use and earn attractive returns from them.

Tesla's focus on robotics is also increasing. The company has repurposed the Model S and Model X production lines at its Fremont factory to scale production of Optimus, its humanoid robot. Tesla ended Model S and Model X production in spring, citing its growing focus on autonomy. The Cybertruck wind-down further reinforces this strategic shift away from some of its existing vehicle programs.

Final Thoughts

Tesla's decision to wind down Cybertruck production makes sense given the truck's weak sales, underutilized capacity and limited progress toward its original volume ambitions. Cybercab has the potential to open up a new market for Tesla, but the company is yet to prove that its autonomous ride-hailing model can work at scale. Optimus is an even longer-term opportunity, with commercial returns still to be demonstrated.

Cybercab may eventually make the shift worthwhile, but until Tesla proves that driverless rides can become a profitable business, the opportunity remains more promise than payoff.

news.Title: Tesla's Texas Robotaxi Fleet Tops Waymo: Should You Get Bullish?
news.Content:
Tesla TSLA has received an encouraging boost to its robotaxi ambitions, reportedly overtaking Alphabet 's GOOGL Waymo in Texas in terms of registered autonomous vehicles. The development strengthens the case for autonomy as an increasingly important growth driver for Tesla. But before getting too excited, investors should remember that expanding a fleet is one thing and building a profitable robotaxi business is another.

Tesla's Texas Fleet Growth Is Hard to Ignore

According to Teslarati, Texas Department of Motor Vehicles records as of Nov. 10 show 1,302 vehicles registered under Tesla Robotaxi, LLC, narrowly ahead of Waymo's 1,297. Tesla's fleet includes 729 Model Y vehicles (accounting for 56% of the total) and 573 purpose-built Cybercabs (44% of the total). Waymo's fleet primarily comprises Jaguar I-PACE vehicles, alongside its newer Zeekr-based Ojai minivans.

The speed of Tesla's expansion is noteworthy. When Texas' autonomous vehicle registry became publicly available in late May 2026, Tesla had just 42 vehicles listed, compared with several hundred for Waymo. Its authorized fleet has since grown more than 30-fold, reflecting substantial Model Y additions and a growing Cybercab presence.

The Cybercab represents a significant milestone for Tesla, as the two-seat vehicle is specifically designed for fully autonomous operation without requiring human intervention. Waymo isn't Tesla's only rival. Amazon 's AMZN Zoox— another purpose-built robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals— has been running paid rides in Las Vegas and is working to bring commercial service to San Francisco and Austin, putting it on a very similar playbook to Cybercab.

Tesla has also been pushing its robotaxi service beyond its original Austin operating area toward San Antonio and Dallas. The company is making progress in turning its autonomy ambitions into an actual service rather than simply showcasing technology.

Why Tesla's Fleet Lead Doesn't Tell the Whole Story

The milestone is encouraging, but fleet numbers alone do not provide the full picture of competitive strength.

For starters, registered vehicles are not necessarily active robotaxis carrying paying passengers. A larger fleet does not automatically translate into more rides, higher utilization or better economics. Also, Alphabet's Waymo operates beyond Texas, making this comparison particularly narrow.

The Cybercab numbers deserve attention, too. Tesla's 573 purpose-built vehicles represent meaningful progress, but Model Y remains the larger part of its fleet. Investors should watch whether future additions increasingly consist of Cybercabs, which would provide a clearer indication that Tesla is scaling its dedicated robotaxi platform.

Story Continues

Ultimately, the bigger opportunity is not simply deploying vehicles but making each one generate meaningful revenues. This requires sufficient passenger demand, frequent rides and a service that can operate reliably across multiple cities.

Tesla's Robotaxi Progress Needs More Proof

Tesla's Texas fleet milestone is promising. Its rapid expansion underscores that the company can deploy vehicles at scale and is making progress toward its autonomy ambitions.

However, getting ahead of Waymo on a state registry is way easier than getting ahead in robotaxi economics. Tesla still needs to demonstrate strong vehicle utilization, sustainable operating economics and successful expansion into additional markets.

The development makes the robotaxi opportunity more credible, but it doesn't really make us bullish on the stock yet. Investors should remain cautiously constructive until Tesla starts showing that its growing fleet can translate into a scalable, profitable business.

news.Title: Morning Bid: Nvidious
news.Content:
By Mike Dolan

Nov 12 (Reuters) - Just when tech stocks looked to be finding their feet again, chip behemoth Nvidia plunged almost 10% overnight on reports its board may now oust troubled CEO Jensen Huang.

The board met late on Wednesday and although there has ‌been no formal announcement yet, the Wall Street Journal reported it was about to remove him.

A potential ouster of Huang, which would ‌set off a flurry of speculation about his replacement with no obvious succession plan in place, comes after he confessed to having an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be spying ​for China.

Pressure mounted further on Wednesday after the New York Times reported a second affair with a more junior Nvidia executive. Political reverberations from the allegations have also rattled the US administration.

If out-of-hours trading is confirmed after the bell today, the cumulative Nvidia share price loss this week would mean well over half a trillion dollars will have been wiped off its market cap.

It would certainly reverse the bounce in its stock and the wider tech sector on Wednesday, when data ‌center firm CoreWeave's battered shares jumped back almost 25% ⁠on a surprising earnings beat. Stock indexes across the world are on the back foot again due to the latest Nvidia twist.

One company that won't thank Nvidia for the timing of all this volatility will be AI giant Anthropic - ⁠currently roadshowing its mega IPO amid shifting sands on its valuation.

Elsewhere, with bond markets closed for Veterans Day on Wednesday, it fell to the dollar to absorb the hot October inflation update and re-upped Federal Reserve rate hike bets, with the greenback's DXY index surging to its highest level since Donald Trump's tariff shock in April ​last ​year.

But even this thinking has been affected by the Nvidia and tech sector turbulence. Yesterday, ​Fed futures had been pricing a small chance of a ‌50-basis-point rate hike next month but that seems to have been removed again overnight in favor of just a quarter-point move.

Otherwise, the big economic release so far on Thursday was a punchy 0.7% rise in Britain's GDP in the third quarter - its fastest growth rate in two years and bringing growth for the year so far to its fastest outside the pandemic in almost a decade.

Once again, even though the lift was broad-based and would be more than 2.5% on an annualized basis, AI-related business activity was cited as one factor despite this year's Iran-related oil price shock.

CHART OF THE DAY

Britain's economy ‌grew at the fastest rate in two-and-a-half years in the third quarter of 2026, helped ​by a boost from AI and extending a strong first half even in the face ​of an oil shock that many had said could trigger recession.

Story Continues

At ​an annualized pace of more than 2.5%, the UK economy is now expanding at its fastest in almost a decade - ‌when the wild swings around the pandemic are stripped out.

news.Title: Ron Baron Says Tesla (TSLA) Could Climb Within a Decade. Ark’s Model Leans on Robotaxis
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA ) ranks 8th on our newly published list of the 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade .

On November 5, the S&P 500 fell 4.36%, its worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash, with roughly $3 trillion in value wiped off S&P 500 companies. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.52% to slip into a correction, and chip stocks took the hardest hit, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling about 12%, its worst day since 2020. The slide followed a rough October, when the technology sector of the S&P 500 lost 6.8%, its biggest monthly drop since March 2025, while defensive groups such as consumer staples had a record month. Growth stocks tend to feel these swings first, because their prices rest on the promise of faster sales and earnings than the rest of the market.

Investors Question the Cost of AI

The worry behind the selling is money. Investors are asking how companies will pay for their enormous artificial intelligence budgets and whether the returns will justify them. The midterm election results added a second concern, as investors began questioning whether the pace of data center construction could slow if new rules follow, which would weigh on AI spending. Our ranking of semiconductor stocks to hold for the next decade covers more of the group that took the sharpest hit.

Why a Ten-Year View Looks Past One Bad Month

A growth stock is a share in a company expected to grow its sales and earnings faster than the market average. These companies usually reinvest profits instead of paying dividends, so shareholders are rewarded through a rising share price, which is why the shares often carry high price-to-earnings ratios. A high multiple is not automatically expensive if the growth keeps coming, but it leaves little room for disappointment, and a stock priced for strong growth can fall sharply when the numbers fall short. Time helps in the other direction, because returns that stay invested earn returns of their own, a snowball effect that builds the longer the money is left alone.

The economy is adding another variable. October's jobs report showed payrolls up 165,000, far above the 65,000 economists expected, and traders now put the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December above 75%. Edward Jones senior global strategist Angelo Kourkafas called it a "blowout jobs report." A strong economy is good for business, but higher interest rates make far-off earnings worth less today, which tends to weigh most on growth stocks. For readers hunting for bargains after the pullback, our list of undervalued growth stocks is a place to start. For long-term holders, the more useful question is not what the market does next month but which companies can keep compounding through several more months like this one.

Story Continues

Tesla qualified as a growth stock mentioned by at least three sources, with a market cap of $1.49 trillion and 116 hedge fund holders in Q2 2026.

Ron Baron, founder of Baron Capital, told CNBC that Tesla could reach $2,000 to $2,500 a share within ten years. Cathie Wood's Ark Invest has published a similar long-range view, a $2,600 target for 2029 that rests on robotaxis supplying nearly 90% of Tesla's enterprise value. Take the robotaxi out, and Ark's own model falls sharply.

The company began giving Robotaxi rides in Cybercabs in Austin late in the quarter, and cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles grew eightfold from the prior quarter, driven by sustained double-digit weekly growth. It ended the period with its largest backlog for passenger vehicles in four years and its highest-ever order rate and backlog in energy storage, a business Tesla says is critical to data center uptime.

Management said battery availability, not demand, was the limit on how many cars it could build, and that it made more progress in securing future supply. If that supply arrives, more of the backlog can turn into deliveries, which is the practical bridge between today's order book and the bigger robotaxi and energy plans long-term holders are waiting on.

Our latest analysis on Tesla (TSLA) is available here: Tesla (TSLA) Needs Stronger Earnings to Justify Its Autonomy Ambitions

While we acknowledge the potential of TSLA as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. If you're looking for an extremely undervalued AI stock that also stands to benefit significantly from Trump-era tariffs and the onshoring trend, see our free report on the best short-term AI stock .

Impressions grew more slowly than price, so the gain came mostly from higher prices rather than more ads. The growth came even as the company kept raising its spending on data centers and servers.

Meta also sees the momentum continuing. It guided fourth-quarter revenue to a range well above the third quarter's level and said it will keep investing aggressively through 2027. About 3.64 billion people use at least one of its apps every day, the audience those AI gains are being applied to.

news.Title: 5 Best Growth Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade
news.Content:
On November 5, the S&P 500 fell 4.36%, its worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash, with roughly $3 trillion in value wiped off S&P 500 companies. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.52% to slip into a correction, and chip stocks took the hardest hit, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling about 12%, its worst day since 2020. The slide followed a rough October, when the technology sector of the S&P 500 lost 6.8%, its biggest monthly drop since March 2025, while defensive groups such as consumer staples had a record month. Growth stocks tend to feel these swings first, because their prices rest on the promise of faster sales and earnings than the rest of the market.

Investors Question the Cost of AI

The worry behind the selling is money. Investors are asking how companies will pay for their enormous artificial intelligence budgets and whether the returns will justify them. The midterm election results added a second concern, as investors began questioning whether the pace of data center construction could slow if new rules follow, which would weigh on AI spending. Our ranking of semiconductor stocks to hold for the next decade covers more of the group that took the sharpest hit.

Why a Ten-Year View Looks Past One Bad Month

A growth stock is a share in a company expected to grow its sales and earnings faster than the market average. These companies usually reinvest profits instead of paying dividends, so shareholders are rewarded through a rising share price, which is why the shares often carry high price-to-earnings ratios. A high multiple is not automatically expensive if the growth keeps coming, but it leaves little room for disappointment, and a stock priced for strong growth can fall sharply when the numbers fall short. Time helps in the other direction, because returns that stay invested earn returns of their own, a snowball effect that builds the longer the money is left alone.

The economy is adding another variable. October's jobs report showed payrolls up 165,000, far above the 65,000 economists expected, and traders now put the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December above 75%. Edward Jones senior global strategist Angelo Kourkafas called it a "blowout jobs report." A strong economy is good for business, but higher interest rates make far-off earnings worth less today, which tends to weigh most on growth stocks. For readers hunting for bargains after the pullback, our list of undervalued growth stocks is a place to start. For long-term holders, the more useful question is not what the market does next month but which companies can keep compounding through several more months like this one.

Story Continues

We shared the expanded list of 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade here. You can find the top 5 stocks below.

Our Methodology

To compile this list, we searched for the best stocks to hold for the next 10 years across investor forums, social media, and financial websites, keeping only growth stocks mentioned by at least three different sources. From those, we picked the 10 with the largest market caps and ranked them in ascending order of market cap. We also list hedge fund holders as of Q2 2026.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? Stanley Druckenmiller's family office has made TSMC its second-largest holding, and he has said he sees "massive disruption" ahead for the chip industry. Cathie Wood's Ark Invest bought more after a strong earnings report, and David Tepper's Appaloosa made it his biggest addition of the second quarter. The pitch is simple: whichever company wins the race to design the best AI processor, it still needs someone to build it.

The latest quarter shows how big that position has become. Revenue was $46.72 billion, up 41.2% in US dollars, and net income rose 68.7%, a record for the sixth straight quarter. High-performance computing, the category that includes AI accelerators, made up 68% of sales. Chief Financial Officer Wendell Huang said the quarter was supported by strong demand for the company's leading-edge process technologies.

Management sees more of the same ahead. TSMC guided fourth-quarter revenue above the third quarter's level, and its newest process technology, 2-nanometer, is already part of the sales mix, with Huang calling the ramp steep. Nvidia guided the current quarter to about $108 billion, and said the outlook assumes no data center compute sales to China. Nvidia says it already holds purchase orders from every major hyperscaler, AI cloud and system maker.

The bulls care most about what comes after. Management gave a preliminary view that revenue for fiscal 2028 will grow about 70%, and described that outlook as limited by supply rather than demand. news.Title: Tesla FSD Gains Ground in Europe: Is EU-Wide Approval Near?
news.Content:
Tesla TSLA is making progress toward expanding its Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology across Europe. Finland has become the 11th European Union (EU) country to grant provisional approval for the system, adding momentum ahead of an EU-wide vote expected next month.

However, national approvals do not guarantee clearance across the bloc. Tesla has won support in several markets but is yet to secure backing from any of the EU's largest member states.

Finland Approval Adds to Tesla's European Momentum

Finland's transport authority, Traficom, fast-tracked its decision, pointing to the changes Tesla has made to the system and the need to give local drivers time to become familiar with it before severe winter conditions.

The changes include reducing the maximum speed offset from 50% to 10% and resetting it to zero every time the vehicle starts. Tesla also renamed its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) technology to Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe.

The name change is significant because regulators have questioned whether the FSD label accurately describes the system's capabilities. Despite its name, the technology does not make a vehicle fully autonomous. Drivers must remain attentive and responsible for the driving task, even when the system assists with steering, acceleration and braking.

Finland's decision follows a series of approvals across Europe, including the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, Czechia, Croatia, Slovakia and Latvia. With Finland joining the list, Tesla now has approvals in 11 EU countries and 19 countries worldwide.

However, several of these European approvals have relied on recognizing the regulatory framework initially established by Dutch authorities. This has helped Tesla expand its footprint, but the broader regulatory challenge remains.

EU-Wide Approval Remains the Bigger Test

Tesla still needs support at the EU level. An approval requires a qualified majority— at least 15 member states representing 65% of the bloc's population.

This is where the lack of support from larger EU economies becomes important. Winning approval in smaller markets is encouraging, but securing backing from major member states will likely be critical to getting the technology cleared across the bloc.

The EU's Technical Committee for Motor Vehicles is expected to decide in December. If approved, the decision could apply across the bloc in about three weeks. A rejection would invalidate the national approvals already granted, making the vote critical to Tesla's European plans.

Story Continues

How Are Other Players Advancing in Autonomy?

The competition in autonomous driving also highlights how different companies are pursuing different paths. Alphabet 's GOOGL Waymo is preparing to bring its driverless ride-hailing service to Munich, Germany, with commercial operations targeted toward the end of 2027, subject to regulatory clearance.

Mobileye MBLY is moving beyond German testing toward planned driverless robotaxi deployments, including a roughly 100-vehicle fleet in Orlando in 2027.

Rivian RIVN is also pursuing supervised autonomy through its Autonomy+ package, including an upcoming Point to Point feature that will navigate a selected route under continuous driver supervision.

Wider FSD Adoption Supports Tesla's Growth

The regulatory push matters to Tesla's effort to build recurring software revenues beyond vehicle sales. Tesla's paid FSD customer base rose 67% year over year to 1.74 million in the third quarter of 2026. More than 75% of new vehicle deliveries in North America included paid FSD subscriptions at delivery. Increasing subscription adoption should strengthen Tesla's software revenues, while wider geographic availability could support vehicle demand and improve long-term profitability.

Access to more markets could widen the customer base and make Tesla vehicles more attractive to buyers interested in driver-assistance features. Still, approvals alone will not ensure subscription growth. Actual adoption will depend on customer willingness to pay, the usefulness of the technology and Tesla's ability to meet local regulatory requirements.

Will National Wins Translate Into EU Approval?

Tesla is making meaningful progress in Europe, and Finland's approval adds to the momentum. However, EU-wide approval is not yet within reach. The lack of backing from major member states remains a hurdle, while the December vote could either validate Tesla's progress or put existing national approvals at risk.

For investors, wider FSD availability offers a promising software revenue opportunity, but it is too early to factor in a broad European rollout. Tesla is getting closer, but the biggest regulatory test is still ahead.
